title.raw: 卷八十八 列傳第五十八 孝友 Volume 88 Biographies 58: Filial Piety

sentences.zh: 序

translations.literal: Preface.
translations.idiomatic: Preface.

sentences.zh: 大矣哉，孝之為德也！

translations.literal: Great indeed is filial piety as a virtue!
translations.idiomatic: How vast is filial devotion as a shaping moral force.

sentences.zh: 分渾元而立體，道貫三靈；

translations.literal: It divides undifferentiated chaos and establishes its substance; the Way penetrates the Three Powers;
translations.idiomatic: From undivided chaos it takes form, and the Way runs through heaven, earth, and humanity.

sentences.zh: 資品匯以順名，功苞萬象。

translations.literal: Drawing on the multitude of kinds to accord with its name, its merit embraces the myriad phenomena.
translations.idiomatic: Grounded in every kind of thing to fit its name, its power embraces all that exists.

sentences.zh: 用之于國，動天地而降休征；

translations.literal: When applied in the state, it moves Heaven and Earth and brings down auspicious omens;
translations.idiomatic: At the level of the state it moves heaven and earth and summons auspicious response.

sentences.zh: 行之於家，感鬼神而昭景福。

translations.literal: When practiced in the family, it affects ghosts and spirits and manifests abundant blessing.
translations.idiomatic: In the household it stirs the spirits and makes lasting good fortune visible.

sentences.zh: 若乃博施備物，尊仁安義，柔色承顏，怡怡盡樂，擊鮮就養，亹癖忘劬，集包思藝黍之勤，循陔有采蘭之詠，事親之道也。

translations.literal: As for broadly dispensing and preparing things, honoring benevolence and settling righteousness, softening one's bearing to please the parents' countenance, sharing harmonious joy to the utmost, slaughtering fresh fare to attend them, tirelessly forgetting one's own toil, gathering millet with the diligence praised in verse, walking the terrace paths to the tune of gathering orchids—these are the ways of serving one's parents.
translations.idiomatic: Then there are those who prepare every provision, uphold humanity and right conduct, soften their manner to please a parent's face, share unstinting delight, bring fresh meat to the table, forget their own fatigue in constant care, labor in the fields as the ode remembers, and pace the paths with the song of orchids—the whole path of honoring father and mother.

sentences.zh: 屬屬如在，哀哀罔極，聚薪流慟，銜索興嗟，曬風樹以隤心，頫寒泉而沫泣，追遠之情也。

translations.literal: Solemnly they seem still present; grief knows no limit; they pile firewood and shed flowing tears; they hold mourning cords and raise sighs; gazing at wind-tossed trees their hearts sink; bowing over cold springs they weep till spittle flies—these are the feelings of honoring the distant dead.
translations.idiomatic: They stand as if the dead were still before them; sorrow without bound moves them to heap fuel and weep aloud, to clutch hemp and lament; the poem of trees in the wind breaks the heart, the spring's chill draws tears—the devotion of those who remember ancestors.

sentences.zh: 審德筮仕，正務移官，居高匪危，在醜無爭，協修升以匡化，懷履冰而砥節，立身之行也。

translations.literal: Carefully weighing virtue and divining office, correcting affairs when transferring posts, dwelling high yet not perilous, among peers engaging in no strife, harmonizing ascent to aid transformation, treading ice to hone one's integrity—these are the deeds of establishing oneself.
translations.idiomatic: They test character before taking office, set duties straight when moved from post, hold rank without arrogance, avoid quarrel among equals, rise in concert with reform, and walk as if on thin ice to temper integrity—the conduct that defines a life.

sentences.zh: 是以閔曾翼翼，遵六教而緝貞規；

translations.literal: Thus Min Sun and Zeng Shen were reverently diligent; they followed the six teachings and knit together steadfast norms;
translations.idiomatic: Hence figures such as Min Sun and Zeng Shen walked with awe through the six teachings and knit an enduring standard.

sentences.zh: 蔡董烝烝，弘七體而垂令跡。

translations.literal: Cai Shun and Dong Yong were harmoniously devoted; they enlarged the seven genres and left admirable traces.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Shun and Dong Yong embodied devoted sons of lore; they fulfilled every virtue on the list and left luminous examples.

sentences.zh: 亦有至誠上感，明祗下贊，郭巨致錫金之慶。

translations.literal: There are also cases where utmost sincerity moved those above and luminous spirits assisted from below, as when Guo Ju brought about the blessing of granted gold.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes sheer sincerity moved heaven and aiding spirits answered below—think of Guo Ju and the gift of gold.

sentences.zh: 陽雍標蒔玉之祉；

translations.literal: Yang Yong marked the auspiciousness of burying a jade;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yong earned the omen of buried jade rewarded;

sentences.zh: 烏馴丹羽，巢叔和之室，鹿呈白毳，擾功文之廬。

translations.literal: Crows with tame red feathers nested in Shu He's chamber; deer showed white fur and tamely approached Gong Wen's hut.
translations.idiomatic: Red crows nested tamely at Shu He's door; white deer grazed calm beside Gong Wen's cottage.

sentences.zh: 然則因彼孝慈而生友悌，理在兼綜，義歸一揆。

translations.literal: Thus from that filial kindness sibling friendship arises; the principle lies in combining both, and the meaning returns to a single measure.
translations.idiomatic: From parental devotion grows brotherly love; the pattern joins both strands, and the moral logic comes to one measure.

sentences.zh: 夫天倫之重，共氣分形，心睽則葉悴荊權，性合則華承棣萼。

translations.literal: As for the weight of natural human bonds, sharing breath yet divided in form—when hearts diverge, leaves wither on bramble branches; when natures unite, blossoms grace the cherry-plum calyx.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven-ordained kin share one breath in separate bodies: estranged hearts leave kin dry as withered leaves; aligned natures flower like blossoms on the same spray.

sentences.zh: 乃有推肥代瘦，徇急難之情；

translations.literal: Moreover there were those who yielded the fat and took the lean in another's place, risking themselves in urgent peril;
translations.idiomatic: Some surrendered the better portion and bore hardship for a brother, staking everything when danger struck;

sentences.zh: 讓果同衾，盡歡愉之致：緬窺緗素，載流塵躅者歟！

translations.literal: Yielding fruit and sharing one cover, they exhausted the utmost of joy and pleasure: gazing far into the silk-bound records, do they not tread as lingering footprints on the dusty track?
translations.idiomatic: They yielded fruit and shared one quilt, tasting every joy brotherhood affords—open those yellowed scrolls and their footprints still seem to stir the dust.

sentences.zh: 晉氏始自中朝，逮于江左，雖百六之災遄及，而君子之道未消，孝悌名流，猶為繼踵。

translations.literal: The Jin house began in the central court and reached the south of the Yangzi; though the calamity of repeated cycles swiftly overtook them, the way of the gentleman was not extinguished, and renowned exemplars of filial piety and fraternal duty still followed one another without cease.
translations.idiomatic: From the central plains down to the southern shore, the Jin endured wave after disaster, yet the gentlemanly way never died; names famed for filial duty followed hard on one another.

sentences.zh: 王偉元之行己，許季義之立節，夏方、盛彥體至性以馳芬，庾袞、顏含篤友于而宣范，自餘群士，咸標懿德。

translations.literal: In the self-conduct of Wang Weiyuan, in the integrity upheld by Xu Jiyi, in Xia Fang and Sheng Yan who embodied utmost nature and spread fragrance, in Yu Gun and Yan Han who were steeped in fraternal brotherhood and proclaimed models—for the rest of the gentlemen as well, each displayed fine virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Weiyuan's bearing, Xu Jiyi's integrity, Xia Fang and Sheng Yan living pure humaneness, Yu Gun and Yan Han modeling brotherly love—the roster runs on, each man a monument of grace.

sentences.zh: 采其遺絢，足厲澆風，故著《孝友篇》以續前史云耳。

translations.literal: Gathering their lingering splendor is enough to sharpen a diluted moral climate; therefore I have compiled this 'Treatise on Filial Piety and Fraternal Duty' to continue the previous histories.
translations.idiomatic: Their lingering brilliance can still stiffen a lax age; I set down this "Filial Friends" chapter to carry the histories forward.

sentences.zh: 李密

translations.literal: Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi

sentences.zh: 李密，字令伯，犍為武陽人也，一名虔。

translations.literal: Li Mi, courtesy name Lingbo, was a native of Wuyang in Qianwei; he had another name, Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi, styled Lingbo, came from Wuyang in Qianwei commandery; he was also known as Qian.

sentences.zh: 父早亡，母何氏醮。

translations.literal: His father died early, and his mother, of the He clan, remarried.
translations.idiomatic: His father died while he was young, and his mother, a Ms. He, remarried.

sentences.zh: 密時年數歲，感戀彌至，烝烝之性，遂以成疾。

translations.literal: Mi was then only a few years old; his feeling and attachment grew extreme, and his devoted nature thus brought on illness.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi was still a small child, yet clung to her so fiercely that his tender devotion turned into sickness.

sentences.zh: 祖母劉氏，躬自撫養，密奉事以孝謹聞。

translations.literal: His paternal grandmother, Lady Liu, personally reared him, and Mi served her with such filial care that he became known for it.
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother Lady Liu raised him herself, and he waited on her so dutifully that his filial name spread.

sentences.zh: 劉氏有疾，則涕泣側息，未嘗解衣，飲膳湯藥必先嘗後進。

translations.literal: When Lady Liu fell ill, he wept and scarcely dared breathe at her side; he never removed his clothes; food, drink, broth, and medicine he always tasted first before presenting them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever she took sick he wept beside her and slept in his clothes; every meal, broth, or dose he tasted himself before she received it.

sentences.zh: 有暇則講學忘疲，而師事譙周，周門人方之游夏。

translations.literal: Whenever he had leisure he lectured and studied, forgetting fatigue; he studied under Qiao Zhou, and Zhou's disciples compared him to Ziyou and Zixia.
translations.idiomatic: In spare moments he studied till weariness vanished; he sat at Qiao Zhou's feet, and fellow students likened him to Confucius's finest disciples.

sentences.zh: 少仕蜀，為郎。

translations.literal: In youth he served Shu as a gentleman-attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Young, he entered Shu service as a court gentleman.

sentences.zh: 數使吳，有才辯，吳人稱之。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly sent on missions to Wu and had eloquence and argument; the people of Wu praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Sent repeatedly to Wu, he debated with polish and won southern acclaim.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，泰始初，詔徵為太子洗馬。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, at the beginning of the Taishi reign an edict summoned him to be attendant groom for the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell, in early Taishi an edict named him groom-purifier to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 密以祖母年高，無人奉養，遂不應命。

translations.literal: Mi, because his grandmother was advanced in age and there was no one to serve and support her, therefore did not answer the summons.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded that his aged grandmother had no one else to care for her and declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 乃上疏曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: He therefore memorialized:

sentences.zh: 帝覽之曰：「士之有名，不虛然哉！

translations.literal: The emperor read it and said, "For a scholar to have such a reputation—it is not empty fame!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and said, "So this is why his name rings true among gentlemen!

sentences.zh: 」乃停召。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he halted the summons.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspended the appointment.

sentences.zh: 後劉終，服闋，復以洗馬徵至洛。

translations.literal: Later when Liu died, when the mourning period was completed, he was again summoned as attendant groom and went to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Lady Liu died and mourning ended, he was summoned again as groom-purifier and traveled to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 司空張華問之曰：「安樂公何如？

translations.literal: Minister of Works Zhang Hua asked him, "How does the Duke of Anle compare?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua asked him, "What do you make of the Duke of Anle?

sentences.zh: 」密曰：「可次齊桓。

translations.literal: " Mi said, "He may be ranked next to Duke Huan of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Mi replied, "Roughly on par with Duke Huan of Qi.

sentences.zh: 」華問其故，對曰：「齊桓得管仲而霸，用豎刁而蟲流。

translations.literal: " Hua asked the reason, and he replied, "Duke Huan of Qi obtained Guan Zhong and became hegemon; employing Shu Diao, maggots streamed from his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Hua pressed why; Li Mi said, "Qi Huan rose with Guan Zhong and rotted with Shu Diao—worms poured from his corpse.

sentences.zh: 安樂公得諸葛亮而抗魏，任黃皓而喪國，是知成敗一也。

translations.literal: The Duke of Anle obtained Zhuge Liang and resisted Wei; employing Huang Hao, he lost the state—thus one knows success and failure follow one pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Anle held Wei at bay with Zhuge Liang and lost his realm to Huang Hao—triumph and ruin turn on the same hinge.

sentences.zh: 」次問：「孔明言教何碎？

translations.literal: " Hua next asked, "Why were Zhuge Liang's teachings so minute?
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Hua went on, "Why did Zhuge Liang lecture so tediously?

sentences.zh: 」密曰：「昔舜、禹、皋陶相與語，故得簡雅；

translations.literal: " Mi said, "In antiquity Shun, Yu, and Gao Yao spoke with one another; hence they could be concise and elegant;
translations.idiomatic: " Li Mi answered, "When Shun, Yu, and Gao Yao spoke among peers, their words stayed spare and refined;

sentences.zh: 《大誥》與凡人言，宜碎。

translations.literal: "The Great Announcement" speaks with ordinary men; it ought to be minute.
translations.idiomatic: the "Great Announcement" addresses plain folk and therefore sounds granular.

sentences.zh: 孔明與言者無己敵，言教是以碎耳。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang had no equal among those who spoke with him; hence his teachings were minute.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang faced listeners who could not match him, so his teaching grew painstakingly detailed.

sentences.zh: 」華善之。

translations.literal: " Hua approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Hua accepted the answer.

sentences.zh: 出為溫令，而憎疾從事，嘗與人書曰：「慶父不死，魯難未已。

translations.literal: He went out as magistrate of Wen, but hated his aide-de-camp; he once wrote someone a letter saying, "If Qing Fu does not die, Lu's calamities will not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Posted magistrate of Wen, he despised his clerk and once wrote a friend, "Until Qing Fu dies, Lu never rests—

sentences.zh: 」從事白其書司隸，司隸以密在縣清慎，弗之劾也。

translations.literal: " The aide reported his letter to the metropolitan inspector; the metropolitan inspector, because Mi was incorrupt and cautious in the county, did not impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: " The clerk denounced the letter to the capital inspector, who left Li Mi untouched because his county rule stayed scrupulous.

sentences.zh: 密有才能，常望內轉，而朝廷無援，乃遷漢中太守，自以失分懷怨。

translations.literal: Mi had talent and ability and constantly hoped for an internal transfer, but the court had no patron for him; he was therefore promoted to governor of Hanzhong and, deeming himself deprived of his proper due, harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Talented and eager for a capital post, he lacked patrons and was shunted to governor of Hanzhong—a posting he resented as a slight.

sentences.zh: 及賜餞東堂，詔密令賦詩，末章曰：「人亦有言，有因有緣。

translations.literal: When he was feasted with a parting gift in the Eastern Hall, an edict ordered Mi to compose a poem; its final stanza said, "People also have a saying: there is cause and there is circumstance.
translations.idiomatic: At a farewell banquet in the Eastern Hall he was told to improvise a poem whose closing lines ran, "As the proverb goes, cause and condition rule our lot.

sentences.zh: 官無中人，不如歸田。

translations.literal: If in office one lacks a go-between at court, one might as well return to the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Without a friend inside the palace, better go home and plow.

sentences.zh: 明明在上，斯語豈然！

translations.literal: Brilliant indeed is he who sits above—could such words be true?
translations.idiomatic: The radiant Son of Heaven reigns on high—would such words stand?

sentences.zh: 」武帝忿之，於是都官從事奏免密官。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wu was angered; thereupon the capital attendant clerk memorialized to dismiss Mi from office.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Wu took offense, and the metropolitan clerk impeached him out of office.

sentences.zh: 後卒於家。

translations.literal: Later he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home in the end.

sentences.zh: 二子：賜、興。

translations.literal: He had two sons: Ci and Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Two sons survived him: Li Ci and Li Xing.

sentences.zh: 賜字宗石，少能屬文，嘗為《玄鳥賦》，詞甚美。

translations.literal: Ci, courtesy name Zongshi, in youth could compose texts; he once wrote "Rhapsody on the Dark Bird," and its diction was very fine.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ci, styled Zongshi, wrote verse early; his "Rhapsody on the Dark Bird" was superbly turned.

sentences.zh: 州辟別駕，舉秀才，未行而終。

translations.literal: The province summoned him as aide-de-camp; he was recommended as cultivated talent, but before taking office he died.
translations.idiomatic: The province wanted him as junior aide and nominated him as "flourishing talent," yet he died before reporting.

sentences.zh: 興字雋石，亦有文才，刺史羅尚辟別駕。

translations.literal: Xing, courtesy name Juanshi, also had literary talent; Inspector Luo Shang summoned him as aide-de-camp.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xing, styled Juanshi, showed the same literary gifts; Governor Luo Shang appointed him aide.

sentences.zh: 尚為李雄所攻，使興詣鎮南將軍劉弘求救，興因願留，為弘參軍而不還。

translations.literal: When Shao was attacked by Li Xiong, he sent Xing to go to General Who Guards the South Liu Hong to seek rescue; Xing then wished to remain and became Hong's army adviser and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: When Luo Shao faced Li Xiong's assault he sent Li Xing south to beg relief from Liu Hong; Li Xing stayed on as Liu Hong's staff adviser and never went back.

sentences.zh: 尚白弘，弘即奪其手版而遣之。

translations.literal: Shao informed Hong; Hong immediately seized his hand tablet and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shao complained to Liu Hong, who seized Li Xing's official tablet and ordered him home.

sentences.zh: 興之在弘府，弘立諸葛孔明、羊叔子碣，使興俱為之文，甚有辭理。

translations.literal: While Xing was in Hong's bureau, Hong erected stone tablets for Zhuge Kongming and Uncle Yang of Yangzhou and had Xing compose texts for both; they had excellent rhetorical logic.
translations.idiomatic: During Li Xing's stay, Liu Hong raised steles to Zhuge Liang and Yang Hu and had Li Xing draft both inscriptions—each tightly argued.

sentences.zh: 盛彥

translations.literal: Sheng Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yan

sentences.zh: 盛彥，字翁子，廣陵人也。

translations.literal: Sheng Yan, courtesy name Wengzi, was a native of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yan, styled Wengzi, came from Guangling.

sentences.zh: 少有異才。

translations.literal: In youth he had unusual talent.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he showed extraordinary gifts.

sentences.zh: 年八歲，詣吳太尉戴昌，昌贈詩以觀之，彥於坐答之。

translations.literal: At age eight he visited Wu's Grand Commandant Dai Chang; Chang presented him with a poem to observe him, and Yan replied while seated.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he called on Grand Commandant Dai Chang of Wu, who handed him a poem as a test; Sheng Yan answered on the spot.

sentences.zh: 辭甚慷慨。

translations.literal: The wording was very impassioned.
translations.idiomatic: His reply rang with generous fervor.

sentences.zh: 母王氏因疾失明，彥每言及，未嘗不流涕。

translations.literal: His mother, of the Wang clan, lost her sight to illness; whenever Yan spoke of it, he never failed to shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Wang went blind from illness; whenever he spoke of her he wept.

sentences.zh: 於是不應辟召，躬自侍養，母食必自哺之。

translations.literal: Therefore he did not answer summons to office but personally attended her; whenever she ate, he invariably fed her with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: He refused every appointment and nursed her himself, spooning every meal to her lips.

sentences.zh: 母既疾久，至於婢使數見捶撻。

translations.literal: Because her illness lasted long, the maidservants repeatedly suffered flogging.
translations.idiomatic: Her long sickness frayed every nerve until he flogged the maids time and again.

sentences.zh: 婢忿恨，伺彥暫行，取蠐螬灸飴之。

translations.literal: The maidservant harbored resentment; watching for when Yan briefly went out, she took grubs, roasted them, and mixed them into sweets.
translations.idiomatic: One maid nursed a grudge; when Sheng Yan stepped out she roasted grubs into the sweets.

sentences.zh: 母食以為美，然疑是異物，密藏以示彥。

translations.literal: The mother ate and thought it delicious, yet suspected it was something strange; she secretly kept some to show Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His mother found it savory yet suspected foul play and hid a sample for her son.

sentences.zh: 彥見之，抱母慟哭，絕而復蘇。

translations.literal: When Yan saw it, he embraced his mother and wailed; he cut off breath and then revived.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw it he clutched his mother and sobbed himself unconscious, then revived.

sentences.zh: 母目豁然即開，從此遂愈。

translations.literal: The mother's eyes suddenly opened clear and from then on she was cured.
translations.idiomatic: Her eyes flew open at once and from that day she healed.

sentences.zh: 彥仕吳，至中書侍郎，吳平，陸雲薦之于刺史周浚，本邑大中正劉頌又舉彥為小中正。

translations.literal: Yan served Wu and rose to palace attendant of the secretariat; when Wu was pacified, Lu Yun recommended him to Inspector Zhou Jun, and the senior rectifier of his native commandery Liu Song further nominated Yan as junior rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: He served Wu as palace secretary cadet; after conquest Lu Yun urged Inspector Zhou Jun to employ him, and local chief classifier Liu Song nominated him junior classifier.

sentences.zh: 太康中卒。

translations.literal: He died during the Taikang era.
translations.idiomatic: He died during Taikang.

sentences.zh: 夏方

translations.literal: Xia Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Fang

sentences.zh: 夏方，字文正，會稽永興人也。

translations.literal: Xia Fang, courtesy name Wenzheng, was a native of Yongxing in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Fang, styled Wenzheng, came from Yongxing in Kuaiji commandery.

sentences.zh: 家遭疫癘，父母伯叔群從死者十三人。

translations.literal: His household suffered pestilence; father, mother, uncles, and cousins—thirteen persons in all—died.
translations.idiomatic: Plague swept his clan: parents, uncles, and cousins—thirteen dead.

sentences.zh: 方年十四，夜則號哭，晝則負土，十有七載，葬送得畢，因廬於墓側，種植松柏，烏鳥猛獸馴擾其旁。

translations.literal: Fang was fourteen; by night he wailed, by day he carried earth—seventeen years until burial was finished; he therefore built a hut beside the graves, planted pines and cypresses, and crows and fierce beasts tamely gathered round.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he keened through nights and hauled soil by day for seventeen years until every burial closed; he hutched beside the tombs, planted evergreens, and found birds and beasts grazing tame at his side.

sentences.zh: 吳時拜仁義都尉，累遷五官中郎將。

translations.literal: Under Wu he was appointed chief commandant of benevolence and righteousness and advanced by stages to general of the Gentlemen of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: Wu named him chief for ritual warriors and later promoted him to captain of the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 朝會未嘗乘車，行必讓路。

translations.literal: At court assemblies he never rode in a carriage; when walking he invariably yielded the road.
translations.idiomatic: At court he never rode; on foot he always stood aside for others.

sentences.zh: 吳平，除高山令。

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified, he was appointed magistrate of Gaoshan.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu fell he became magistrate of Gaoshan.

sentences.zh: 百姓有罪應加捶撻者，方向之涕泣而不加罪，大小莫敢犯焉。

translations.literal: When commoners had offenses that should have received beating and flogging, Fang would weep before them and not inflict punishment; young and old none dared offend.
translations.idiomatic: When townsfolk deserved the rod he wept until punishment seemed cruel and forgave them all—none dared sin twice.

sentences.zh: 在官三年，州舉秀才，還家，卒，年八十七。

translations.literal: After three years in office the province recommended him as cultivated talent; he returned home and died at age eighty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Three years into office the province nominated him as "flourishing talent"; he went home and died at eighty-seven.

sentences.zh: 王裒

translations.literal: Wang Pou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pou

sentences.zh: 王裒，字偉元，城陽營陵人也。

translations.literal: Wang Pou, courtesy name Weiyuan, was a native of Yingling in Chengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pou, styled Weiyuan, came from Yingling in Chengyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖修，有名魏世。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xiu had renown in the Wei era.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wang Xiu had been celebrated under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父儀，高亮雅直，為文帝司馬。

translations.literal: His father Yi was lofty, bright, refined, and upright, and served Emperor Wen as marshal.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Yi—lofty, blunt, and upright—had served Emperor Wen of Wei as chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 東關之役，帝問於眾曰：「近日之事，誰任其咎？

translations.literal: At the battle of Dongguan the emperor asked the assembly, "In recent affairs, who bears the blame?
translations.idiomatic: During the Dongguan battle Emperor Wen asked his officials, "Who owns this recent defeat?

sentences.zh: 」儀對曰：「責在元帥。

translations.literal: " Yi replied, "The responsibility lies with the commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Yi answered, "Blame rests with the supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 」帝怒曰：「司馬欲委罪於孤邪！

translations.literal: " The emperor angrily said, "Does the marshal intend to shift blame onto me?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor snapped, "Do you mean to hang this on your sovereign?

sentences.zh: 」遂引出斬之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he had him led out and executed.
translations.idiomatic: " He had Wang Yi dragged out and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 裒少立操尚，行己以禮，身長八尺四寸，容貌絕異，音聲清亮，辭氣雅正，博學多能，痛父非命，未嘗西向而坐。

translations.literal: Pou in youth established conduct and aspirations; he regulated himself with ritual; he stood eight chi four cun tall; his appearance was surpassingly unusual; his voice was clear and bright; his phrasing and bearing were refined and correct; he was broadly learned and greatly capable; grieving his father's unnatural death, he never sat facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Young Wang Pou formed stern principles and lived by ritual—tall, striking, voice clear, speech measured, learned in many arts; mourning his father's unjust death he never sat facing west.

sentences.zh: 示不臣朝廷也。

translations.literal: This showed he did not serve the court as subject.
translations.idiomatic: He refused ever to turn toward Luoyang's throne.

sentences.zh: 於是隱居教授，三征七辟皆不就。

translations.literal: Thereupon he lived in reclusion teaching; three summonses and seven recruitments he none accepted.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to teach privately and thrice spurned summonses, seven times refusing appointments.

sentences.zh: 廬于墓側，旦夕常至墓所拜跪，攀柏悲號，涕淚著樹，樹為之枯。

translations.literal: He built a hut beside the tomb; morning and evening he constantly came to the grave site to bow and kneel; grasping the cypress he wailed in grief; tears fell on the trees so that the trees withered from it.
translations.idiomatic: He hutched beside her grave, bowing morning and night, clutching the cypress until his tears soaked the bark and the trees died.

sentences.zh: 母性畏雷，母沒，每雷，輒到墓曰：「裒在此。

translations.literal: His mother's nature feared thunder; after his mother died, whenever there was thunder he would go to the tomb and say, "Pou is here.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had feared thunder; after she died he hurried to the mound at every peal and cried, "Your son Pou is here.

sentences.zh: 」及讀《詩》至「哀哀父母，生我劬勞」，未嘗不三復流涕，門人受業者並廢《蓼莪》之篇。

translations.literal: " And when he read the Classic of Poetry to the lines "Alas for father and mother, who toiled to rear me," he never failed to repeat them thrice with flowing tears; disciples receiving instruction altogether abandoned the "Luxuriant Motherwort" piece.
translations.idiomatic: " Whenever lessons touched "How bitterly I cry for father and mother" he wept through three readings, so students skipped the "Motherwort" ode altogether.

sentences.zh: 家貧，躬耕，計口而田，度身而蠶。

translations.literal: His household was poor; he personally ploughed, reckoning fields by mouths and mulberry by bodies.
translations.idiomatic: Poor, he worked his own fields—measuring seed to mouths and silk to bodies.

sentences.zh: 或有助之者，不聽。

translations.literal: When some wished to assist him, he did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone offering help he politely refused.

sentences.zh: 諸生密為刈麥，裒遂棄之。

translations.literal: The disciples secretly cut wheat for him; Pou therefore cast it away.
translations.idiomatic: Students once harvested wheat for him in secret; he dumped every kernel rather than accept.

sentences.zh: 知舊有致遺者，皆不受。

translations.literal: When old acquaintances sent gifts, he refused them all.
translations.idiomatic: He turned away every gift from old friends.

sentences.zh: 門人為本縣所役，告裒求屬令，裒曰：「卿學不足以庇身，吾德薄不足以廕卿，屬之何益！

translations.literal: A disciple was pressed into labor by the county; he told Pou and asked him to ask the magistrate for favor. Pou said, "Your learning is not enough to shelter your person; my virtue is thin and not enough to extend protection to you—what good would a recommendation do!
translations.idiomatic: When a pupil faced county corvée and begged Wang Pou to intercede with the magistrate, Wang said, "Your scholarship cannot shield you; my thin virtue cannot shade you—what use is pulling strings?

sentences.zh: 且吾不執筆已四十年矣。

translations.literal: Moreover I have not lifted the brush myself for forty years.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, I have not written for anyone in forty years.

sentences.zh: 」乃步擔乾飯，兒負鹽豉草屐，送所役生到縣，門徒隨從者千餘人。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he walked, carrying dried rice on a shoulder pole, his son bearing salt, fermented beans, and straw sandals, and escorted the conscripted disciple to the county seat; disciples who followed numbered over a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Then he hoisted dried rations on a shoulder pole while his son lugged salt, bean relish, and straw sandals, and walked the drafted pupil to the yamen with more than a thousand students trailing behind.

sentences.zh: 安丘令以為詣己，整衣出迎之。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Anqiu thought Pou was coming to pay him a visit; he straightened his robes and went out to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: The Anqiu magistrate assumed the visit was for him, dressed formally, and hurried out to greet Wang Pou.

sentences.zh: 裒乃下道至土牛旁，磬折而立，云：「門生為縣所役，故來送別。

translations.literal: Pou then stepped off the road beside the earthen ox, bowed deeply at the waist, and said, "My disciple was pressed into county labor; therefore I have come to bid him farewell.
translations.idiomatic: Wang stepped aside by the clay ox, bowed low, and said only, "My student labors for the county—I came to see him off.

sentences.zh: 」因執手涕泣而去。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he took him by the hand, weeping, and took his leave.
translations.idiomatic: He clasped hands, wept, and walked away.

sentences.zh: 令即放之，一縣以為恥。

translations.literal: The magistrate immediately released the disciple; the whole county regarded it as a shame.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate freed the man at once, and the county squirmed at its own pettiness.

sentences.zh: 鄉人管彥少有才而未知名，裒獨以為必當自達，拔而友之，男女各始生，便共許為婚。

translations.literal: His fellow townsman Guan Yan had talent in youth but was not yet known; Pou alone believed he would surely rise of himself, lifted him up and befriended him; when each had fathered a boy and a girl at birth, they jointly pledged them in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Townsmen Guan Yan had talent but no fame until Wang Pou singled him out, befriended him, and betrothed their infant son and daughter while still in the cradle.

sentences.zh: 彥後為西夷校尉，卒而葬於洛陽，裒後更嫁其女。

translations.literal: Later Yan became Colonel Who Pacifies the Yi; when he died he was buried at Luoyang, and Pou later married off his daughter elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yan rose to western frontier colonel and was buried at Luoyang; Wang Pou later gave his daughter to another house.

sentences.zh: 彥弟馥問裒，裒曰：「吾薄志畢願山藪，昔嫁姊妹皆遠，吉凶斷絕，每以此自誓。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Fu asked Pou; Pou said, "My humble ambition has always been to finish my days in mountain wilds; in the past when I married off sisters they went far away and fortune and misfortune broke off contact—I have sworn by that often.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Fu pressed him; Wang Pou explained that he meant to end his days in the hills, that sisters wed far away had lost touch through joy and sorrow, and he had sworn never to bind children to the capital.

sentences.zh: 今賢兄子葬於洛陽。

translations.literal: Now your worthy elder brother's son is buried at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Your nephew now lies buried in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 此則京邑之人也，由吾結好之本意哉！

translations.literal: That makes him a man of the capital region—how does that match the intent with which I originally formed the marriage tie!
translations.idiomatic: That ties him to the capital—nothing like the rustic match I intended.

sentences.zh: 」馥曰：「嫂，齊人也，當還臨淄。

translations.literal: " Fu said, "My sister-in-law is a person of Qi; she ought to return to Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu answered, "His mother is a Qi woman—she belongs back in Linzi.

sentences.zh: 」裒曰：「安有葬父河南而隨母還齊！

translations.literal: " Pou said, "How can there be burying a father south of the Yellow River yet following the mother back to Qi!
translations.idiomatic: " Wang shot back, "Who buries a father in Henan yet trails mother to Qi?

sentences.zh: 用意如此，何婚之有！」

translations.literal: When intentions run like this, what marriage tie remains!"
translations.idiomatic: With motives like that, what alliance is left?"

sentences.zh: 北海邴春少立志操，寒苦自居，負笈遊學，鄉邑僉以為邴原復出。

translations.literal: Bing Chun of Beihai in youth set his mind on conduct; he embraced hardship of his own accord, carried a book-box and wandered studying; the township unanimously thought Bing Yuan had come again.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Chun of Beihai embraced austerity and wandered with books on his back until locals swore Bing Yuan had been reborn.

sentences.zh: 裒以春性險狹慕名，終必不成。

translations.literal: Pou considered that Chun's nature was narrow and peril-seeking and pursued fame; in the end he would not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pou judged him restless and fame-hungry—he would come to nothing.

sentences.zh: 其後春果無行，學業不終，有識以此歸之。

translations.literal: Afterward Chun indeed lacked conduct; his studies did not finish; men of judgment on this account credited Pou.
translations.idiomatic: Chun later proved faithless and dropped his studies—thoughtful men credited Wang Pou's foresight.

sentences.zh: 裒常以為人之所行期於當歸善道，何必以所能而責人所不能。

translations.literal: Pou constantly held that what people practice should aim at returning to the good way—why use what one can do to blame others for what they cannot.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pou felt conduct should bend toward the good—never judge others by talents they lack.

sentences.zh: 及洛京傾覆，寇資蜂起，親族悉欲移渡江東，裒戀墳壟不去。

translations.literal: When the Luoyang capital collapsed and bandit supplies swarmed forth, kinsmen all wished to move east across the Yangzi; Pou clung to the graves and mounds and would not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell and rebels multiplied, kin fled toward the eastern Jin redoubt, but Wang Pou stayed by the tombs.

sentences.zh: 賊大盛，方行，猶思慕不能進，遂為賊所害。

translations.literal: When the bandits grew strong he finally set out, yet still longed and yearned and could not advance; thereupon he was killed by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When robbers closed in he tried to flee yet lingered at the graves until they cut him down.

sentences.zh: 許孜

translations.literal: Xu Zi.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zi

sentences.zh: 許孜，字季義，東陽吳寧人也。

translations.literal: Xu Zi, courtesy name Jiyi, was a native of Wuning in Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zi, styled Jiyi, came from Wuning in Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 孝友恭讓，敏而好學。

translations.literal: He was filial, friendly, deferential, and yielding; keen and fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Filial, gentle, courteous, and eager to learn.

sentences.zh: 年二十，師事豫章太守會稽孔沖，受《詩》、《書》、《禮》、《易》及《孝經》、《論語》。

translations.literal: At twenty he studied under Governor of Yuzhang Kong Chong of Kuaiji, receiving the "Classic of Poetry," "Documents," "Rites," "Changes," as well as "Classic of Filial Piety" and "Analects."
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he studied under Kong Chong, governor of Yuzhang, mastering the Poetry, Documents, Rites, Changes, Filial Piety, and Analects.

sentences.zh: 學竟，還鄉里。

translations.literal: When his studies finished, he returned to his village.
translations.idiomatic: When coursework ended he went home.

sentences.zh: 沖在郡喪亡，孜聞問盡哀，負擔奔赴，送喪還會稽，蔬食執役，制服三年。

translations.literal: When Chong died in office, upon hearing the news Zi exhausted his grief; shouldering a pack he hurried off, escorted the funeral back to Kuaiji, ate vegetable fare and performed labor, observing mourning garments for three years.
translations.idiomatic: When Kong Chong died in post, Xu Zi raced to the funeral, carried the coffin to Kuaiji, ate plain food, served like a laborer, and mourned three years.

sentences.zh: 俄而二親沒，柴毀骨立，杖而能起，建墓於縣之東山，躬自負土，不受鄉人之助。

translations.literal: Soon both parents died; he wasted away until only bones stood; with a staff he could rise; he built tombs on the eastern hill of the county, carried earth on his own back, and accepted no help from fellow villagers.
translations.idiomatic: When both parents died he grew skeletal yet rose with a cane; he piled tombs on the eastern hill, hauling soil alone and refusing neighbors' aid.

sentences.zh: 或湣孜羸憊，苦求來助，孜晝助不逆，夜便除之。

translations.literal: Some pitied Zi's exhaustion and bitterly begged to come help; Zi by day did not refuse when they assisted, but by night removed what they had done.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors pitied his exhaustion and insisted on helping; he let them work by day but tore their work down overnight.

sentences.zh: 每一悲號，鳥獸翔集。

translations.literal: Whenever he gave voice to grief, birds and beasts hovered aloft and gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he wailed, birds and beasts flocked in as if answering his cry.

sentences.zh: 孜以方營大功，乃棄其妻，鎮宿墓所，列植松柏亙五六里。

translations.literal: Zi, because he was about to perform the great rites, set aside his wife, lodged by night at the grave, and planted pines and cypress in rows five or six li long.
translations.idiomatic: He set aside his wife to keep the great mourning, slept at the tumulus, and lined the hills with pines and cypress for miles.

sentences.zh: 時有鹿犯其松栽，改悲歎曰：「鹿獨不念我乎！

translations.literal: At times a deer trampled his pine saplings; Zi grieved and sighed, "Does the deer alone show no care for me!
translations.idiomatic: When a deer broke his saplings he cried, "Have you no pity for me?

sentences.zh: 」明日，忽見鹿為猛獸所殺，置於所犯栽下。

translations.literal: The next day he suddenly saw the deer killed by a fierce beast and laid beneath the saplings it had harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Next morning he found the deer torn by some beast and laid under the same seedlings.

sentences.zh: 孜悵惋不已，乃為作塚，埋於隧側。

translations.literal: Zi was endlessly sorrowful; therefore he fashioned a grave mound for it and buried it beside the tomb passage.
translations.idiomatic: Heartbroken, he dug a grave beside the path and buried the deer.

sentences.zh: 猛獸即於孜前自撲而死，孜益歎息，又取埋之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the fierce beast collapsed dead before Zi; Zi sighed yet more and took it also and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: Then a predator dropped dead at his feet—he buried that beast too, sighing still deeper.

sentences.zh: 自後樹木滋茂，而無犯者。

translations.literal: Afterward the trees grew thick and luxuriant, and none again intruded on them.
translations.idiomatic: The grove grew thick, and no animal ever trampled it again.

sentences.zh: 積二十餘年孜乃更娶妻，立宅墓次，烝烝朝夕，奉亡如存，鷹雉棲其梁，簷鹿與猛獸擾其庭圃，交頸同遊，不相搏噬。

translations.literal: More than twenty years passed before Zi took another wife; he built a house beside the tomb, cherishing morning and evening, serving the dead as if they lived; hawks and pheasants nested on his beams; deer and fierce beasts tamely roamed his courtyard and garden; they walked together with necks entwined and did not attack one another.
translations.idiomatic: Only after two decades did he remarry, building a house at the grave and serving the dead as if alive; hawks and pheasants nested in his rafters, deer and predators mingled in the yard without strife.

sentences.zh: 元康中，郡察孝廉，不起，巾褐終身。

translations.literal: During Yuankang the province recommended him as filial and incorrupt; he did not take office, wearing headcloth and brown robe to the end of his life.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuankang years the province cited him as filial and honest, but he never took office, spending life in homespun.

sentences.zh: 年八十餘，卒於家。

translations.literal: At more than eighty years of age he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home in his eighties.

sentences.zh: 邑人號其居為孝順裏。

translations.literal: Townsmen called his residence "Filial Hamlet."
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors called his lane the Hamlet of Filial Sons.

sentences.zh: 咸康中，太守張虞上疏曰：「臣聞聖賢明訓存乎舉善，褒貶所興，不遠千載。

translations.literal: During Xiankang Prefect Zhang Yu submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject has heard that the clear teaching of sages rests in exalting the good; that praise and blame arouse men though a thousand years lie between.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiankang, Prefect Zhang Yu wrote, "Sages teach us to exalt the good; their praise and blame still echo a millennium on.

sentences.zh: 謹案所領吳甯縣物故人許孜，至性孝友，立節清峻，與物恭讓，言行不貳。

translations.literal: Respectfully I have reviewed the man of this commandery, the late native Xu Zi, who in utmost nature was filial and friendly, who set up integrity clear and severe, who toward others was deferential and yielding, and in word and act was without duplicity.
translations.idiomatic: I review Wuning’s late Xu Zi—utterly filial, upright, humble, and consistent in word and deed.

sentences.zh: 當其奉師，則在三之義盡；

translations.literal: In serving his teacher he fulfilled the duty of the "three" among the many relationships;
translations.idiomatic: Honoring his master he met every duty the “threes” require of a pupil;

sentences.zh: 及其喪親，實古今之所難。

translations.literal: In burying his parents he achieved what is hard for both ancient and modern times.
translations.idiomatic: Burying his parents he did what few ancients or moderns could match.

sentences.zh: 咸稱殊類致感，猛獸弭害。

translations.literal: All agreed that different species were moved and fierce beasts put away harm.
translations.idiomatic: All said wild things bowed to him and savage beasts forgot to harm.

sentences.zh: 雖臣不及見，然備聞斯語，竊謂蔡順、董黯無以過之。

translations.literal: Though your subject did not witness it in person, having fully heard these words, your subject privately judges that Cai Shun and Dong Yin could not surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: I did not witness it, yet the accounts make Cai Shun and Dong Yin look no greater.

sentences.zh: 孜沒積年，其子尚在，性行純愨，今亦家於墓側。

translations.literal: Many years after Zi died his son is still living; his nature and conduct are pure and devoted; now he also dwells beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Long after Xu Zi’s death his son still lives in pure piety, keeping house by the grave.

sentences.zh: 臣以為孜之履操，世所希逮，宜標其令跡，甄其後嗣，以酬既往，以獎方來。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that Zi's practice is what the age rarely attains; it is fitting to mark his excellent traces and advance his posterity, thereby requiting the past and encouraging what is to come.
translations.idiomatic: Such conduct is matchless; the court should ennoble his name and free his heirs to reward the past and teach the future.

sentences.zh: 《陽秋傳》曰：'善善及其子孫'。

translations.literal: The Chunqiu says: 'When you reward goodness, reach to sons and grandsons.'
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo tradition says, 'When you honor goodness, bless the next generation too.'

sentences.zh: 臣不達大體，請台量議。

translations.literal: Your subject does not understand great measures; I beg the bureaus to measure and discuss.
translations.idiomatic: I am unfit to decide the rites; let the ministry rule on it.

sentences.zh: 」疏奏，詔旌表門閭。

translations.literal: When the memorial was presented, an edict ordered the gate honored with a posted banner.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved the memorial and ordered a honorific plaque for his gate.

sentences.zh: 蠲復子孫。

translations.literal: Remission of corvée for sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: His descendants were excused from labor service.

sentences.zh: 其子生亦有孝行。

translations.literal: His son likewise practiced filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His son showed the same filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 圖孜像於堂，朝夕拜焉。

translations.literal: He painted Zi's likeness in the hall and bowed to it morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: He hung a portrait of Xu Zi in the hall and bowed to it daily.

sentences.zh: 庾袞

translations.literal: Yu Gun.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Gun

sentences.zh: 庾袞，字叔褒，明穆皇后伯父也。

translations.literal: Yu Gun, courtesy name Shubao, was the paternal uncle of Empress Dowager Mingmu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Gun, styled Shubao, was the Empress Mingmu’s uncle on her father’s side.

sentences.zh: 少履勤儉，篤學好問，事親以孝稱。

translations.literal: In youth he practiced diligence and frugality, was devoted to learning and fond of inquiry, and served his parents, famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He grew up frugal, bookish, and already praised for filial care.

sentences.zh: 咸寧中，大疫，二兄俱亡，次兄毗復殆，癘氣方熾，父母諸弟皆出次於外，袞獨留不去。

translations.literal: During Xianning a great pestilence came; both elder brothers died one after another; the next brother Pi was again at the point of death; the miasma was still fierce; parents and younger brothers all moved out to lodge outside, but Gun alone remained and would not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianning plague both elder brothers died; a third, Pi, lay near death while the miasma raged, so parents and brothers fled the house—only Yu Gun stayed.

sentences.zh: 諸父兄強之，乃曰：「袞性不畏病。

translations.literal: His uncles and elder brothers forced him; he then said, "By nature I do not fear disease.
translations.idiomatic: Kinsmen tried to drag him away; he said, "I am not afraid of sickness.

sentences.zh: 」遂親自扶持，晝夜不眠，其間復撫柩哀臨不輟。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he personally supported Pi, day and night without sleep; in the interval he also embraced the coffins and mourned without cease.
translations.idiomatic: " He nursed Pi without sleeping, pausing only to beat his breast beside the coffins.

sentences.zh: 如此十有餘旬，疫勢既歇，家人乃反，毗病得差，袞亦無恙。

translations.literal: Thus for more than a hundred days the epidemic tide ebbed; then the family returned; Pi recovered from illness, and Gun likewise remained unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: After three months the plague broke; the family returned, Pi lived, and Yu Gun never sickened.

sentences.zh: 父老咸曰：「異哉此子！

translations.literal: The village elders all said, "Strange is this young man!
translations.idiomatic: Village elders marveled, "What manner of youth is this?

sentences.zh: 守人所不能守，行人所不能行，歲寒然後知松柏之後凋，始疑疫癘之不相染也。」

translations.literal: He guarded what others cannot guard, practiced what others cannot practice—only when the year turns cold do we know the pine and cypress are last to wither; now we begin to doubt that plague air does not infect one another."
translations.idiomatic: He stayed where others fled and endured what others could not—cold winters reveal which trees stay green; maybe foul vapors spare the steadfast after all."

sentences.zh: 初，袞諸父並貴盛，惟父獨守貧約。

translations.literal: Earlier Gun's uncles had all been prosperous and eminent; only his father kept poverty and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: His uncles lived rich and prominent lives while his father alone stayed poor.

sentences.zh: 袞躬親稼穡，以給供養，而執事勤恪，與弟子樹籬，跪以授條。

translations.literal: Gun personally farmed to supply his parents' needs; in performing labor he was diligent and respectful; when with disciples planting hedgerows he knelt to hand them the slips.
translations.idiomatic: He farmed to feed his parents, worked like a servant, and knelt to pass wicker slips when planting hedges with students.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「今在隱屏，先生何恭之過？

translations.literal: Someone said, "Now we are in private quarters—why, sir, such excessive deference?
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked why he knelt even in private—“why such ceremony?”

sentences.zh: 」袞曰：「幽顯易操，非君子之志也。

translations.literal: " Gun said, "To change deportment between hidden and manifest is not the aspiration of a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu Gun answered, "The gentleman does not shift manners between private rooms and public hall.

sentences.zh: 」父亡，作筥賣以養母。

translations.literal: " When his father died he made baskets to sell and thereby nourish his mother.
translations.idiomatic: " After his father died he wove baskets for coin to feed his mother.

sentences.zh: 母見其勤，曰：「我無所食。

translations.literal: His mother saw his labor and said, "I have nothing to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing him strain, his mother said she could not eat.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「母食不甘，袞將何居！

translations.literal: He replied, "If my mother cannot eat with pleasure, where shall Gun dwell!
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "If you cannot enjoy a meal, how can I go on living?

sentences.zh: 」母感而安之。

translations.literal: " The mother was moved and became at peace.
translations.idiomatic: " She wept and found peace again.

sentences.zh: 袞前妻荀氏，繼妻樂氏，皆官族富室，及適袞，俱棄華麗，散資財，與袞共安貧苦，相敬如賓。

translations.literal: Gun's first wife was of the Xun clan, his second wife of the Yue clan—both were from official great houses and wealthy families; but when they married Gun they both cast aside finery, distributed their property, and with Gun together embraced poverty and hardship, treating one another with the respect of guests.
translations.idiomatic: Two wives from great houses married down to his hovel, shed silks, shared their dowries, and lived in mutual respect like honored guests.

sentences.zh: 母終，服喪居於墓側。

translations.literal: When his mother died he observed mourning and dwelt beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he hutched the grave through mourning.

sentences.zh: 歲大饑，藜羹不糝，門人欲進其飯者，而袞每曰已食，莫敢為設。

translations.literal: In a year of great famine even purslane broth lacked grain grit; disciples wished to bring him rice, but Gun each time said he had already eaten, so none dared prepare food for him.
translations.idiomatic: In famine even weed soup lacked grain; students offered rice, yet he always claimed to have eaten already.

sentences.zh: 及麥熟，獲者已畢，而采捃尚多，袞乃引其群子以退，曰「待其間。

translations.literal: When the wheat ripened, those who harvested had finished, yet gleanings remained plentiful; Gun then led his sons and nephews back and said, "Wait for an interval.
translations.idiomatic: After reapers finished he waited until gleaners moved on, then told sons and nephews to wait their turn.

sentences.zh: 」及其捃也，不曲行，不旁掇，跪而把之，則亦大獲，又與邑人入山拾橡，分夷險，序長幼，推易居難，禮無違者。

translations.literal: " When they gleaned they did not bend to crooked paths nor gather from the sides; kneeling they gathered handfuls and thereby still harvested greatly; again he entered the hills with townsfolk to gather oak nuts; assigning steep and easy slopes and ordering elder and younger, he yielded easy routes and took hard ones—through all he violated no propriety.
translations.idiomatic: " They walked straight rows, knelt to scoop fallen ears, and filled sacks honorably; gathering acorns in the hills they ranked age before youth and claimed the stony slopes themselves.

sentences.zh: 或有斬其墓柏，莫知其誰，乃召鄰人集於墓而自責焉，因叩頭泣涕，謝祖禰曰：「德之不修，不能庇先人之樹，袞之罪也。

translations.literal: Someone felled the pine at his tomb but none knew who; therefore he summoned neighbors to assemble at the tomb and blamed himself, whereupon he knocked his head and weeping addressed grandfather and father: "Unable to cultivate virtue, I could not protect the trees of the ancestors—Gun's offense.
translations.idiomatic: When someone cut his tomb pines he gathered neighbors, blamed himself aloud, and apologized to his ancestors for failing to shelter their grove.

sentences.zh: 」父老咸亦為之垂泣，自後人莫之犯。

translations.literal: " The village elders also wept for him; afterward none offended against him.
translations.idiomatic: " Elders wept with him, and no one touched the trees again.

sentences.zh: 撫諸孤以慈，奉諸寡以仁，事加於厚而教之義方，使長者體其行，幼者忘其孤。

translations.literal: He nurtured orphans with kindness and widowed sisters-in-law with humanity; he treated them with added generosity and instructed them in proper norms, so that elders embodied his conduct and youngsters forgot they were orphaned.
translations.idiomatic: He raised orphans gently and widowed sisters-in-law generously, teaching propriety until elders imitated him and children forgot their loss.

sentences.zh: 孤甥郭秀，比諸子侄，衣食而每先之。

translations.literal: His orphaned nephew Guo Xiu he ranked alongside sons and nephews for clothing and food yet always gave him the better portion first.
translations.idiomatic: He clothed and fed nephew Guo Xiu alongside his own sons yet always served the boy first.

sentences.zh: 孤兄女曰芳，將嫁，美服既具，袞乃刈荊苕為箕帚，召諸子集之於堂，男女以班，命芳曰：「芳乎！

translations.literal: His orphaned niece Fang was about to marry; fine garments were ready; Gun then cut kudzu stalks for dust-baskets and brooms, assembled sons and daughters in the hall by rank of sex, and commanded Fang, "Fang!
translations.idiomatic: When niece Fang married he carved vine baskets instead of silks, lined kin in the hall, and began:

sentences.zh: 汝少孤，汝逸汝豫，不汝疵瑕。

translations.literal: You grew up fatherless; you lived at ease and indulgent; they did not reproach your faults.
translations.idiomatic: You lost your father young yet lived lightly—family overlooked every flaw.

sentences.zh: 今汝適人，將事舅姑，灑掃庭內，婦之道也，故賜汝此。

translations.literal: Now you marry out and will serve parents-in-law and sweep the courtyard—such is a wife's duty; therefore I grant you these.
translations.idiomatic: Now you wed—tending parents-in-law and sweeping courts is a wife’s way—so take these humble tools.

sentences.zh: 匪器之為美，欲溫恭朝夕，雖休勿休也。

translations.literal: It is not that the implements are fine—I desire respectful diligence morning and night; though there be ease, do not indulge ease.
translations.idiomatic: They are not ornaments but reminders to stay humble and diligent every dawn and dusk.

sentences.zh: 」而以舊宅與其長兄子賡、翕。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he gave the old residence to his eldest brother's sons Geng and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he deeded the old house to his nephews Geng and Xi.

sentences.zh: 及翕卒，袞哀其早孤，痛其成人而未娶，乃撫柩長號，哀感行路，聞者莫不垂涕。

translations.literal: When Xi died Gun grieved his early orphanhood and mourned that he had grown to adulthood yet taken no wife; therefore he embraced the coffin and wailed long; travelers along the road shed tears and none who heard failed to weep.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi died young he hugged the coffin and keened until passersby wept.

sentences.zh: 初，袞父誡袞以酒，每醉，輒自責曰：「余廢先父之誡，其何以訓人！

translations.literal: Earlier Gun's father had warned Gun against wine; whenever drunk he would blame himself, saying, "I violate my late father's prohibition—how shall I instruct others!
translations.idiomatic: His father had forbidden wine; drunk once he scourged himself for betraying the lesson.

sentences.zh: 」乃于父墓前自杖三十。

translations.literal: " Thereupon before his father's tomb he beat himself thirty blows with a staff.
translations.idiomatic: " Before his father’s grave he flogged himself thirty strokes.

sentences.zh: 鄰人褚德逸者，善事其親，老而不倦，袞每拜之。

translations.literal: Among neighbors Chu Deyi was good at serving his parents and in old age never slackened; Gun invariably bowed to him.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbor Chu Deyi nursed aged parents without tiring—Yu Gun bowed low whenever they met.

sentences.zh: 嘗與諸兄過邑人陳准兄弟，諸兄友之，皆拜其母，袞獨不拜。

translations.literal: Once when passing townsman Chen Zhun's household with several elder brothers, the brothers befriended them and all bowed to Chen's mother; Gun alone did not bow.
translations.idiomatic: Visiting the Chen brothers with kin, everyone bowed to their mother except Yu Gun.

sentences.zh: 准弟徽曰：「子不拜吾親何？

translations.literal: Zhun's younger brother Hui said, "Why do you not bow to my kin?
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hui demanded why he withheld respect.

sentences.zh: 」袞曰：「未知所以拜也。

translations.literal: " Gun said, "I do not yet know the reason to bow.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu Gun answered, "I saw no ground for such a bow.

sentences.zh: 夫拜人之親者，將自同於人之子也，其義至重，袞敢輕之乎？

translations.literal: Those who bow to others' parents intend to align themselves as others' sons—the moral weight is utmost; how dare Gun treat it lightly?
translations.idiomatic: Prostrating before another’s parents means adopting their son’s place—that obligation dwarfs ordinary courtesy.

sentences.zh: 」遂不拜。

translations.literal: " Therefore he did not bow.
translations.idiomatic: " So he stayed upright.

sentences.zh: 准、徽歎曰：「古有亮直之士，君近之矣。

translations.literal: Zhun and Hui sighed, "The ancients had upright and straightforward gentlemen—you approach them.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen brothers sighed that such stubborn integrity belonged to antiquity.

sentences.zh: 君若當朝，則社稷之臣歟！

translations.literal: Were you to hold court office, you would be a pillar-of-state minister!
translations.idiomatic: Were he to serve at court he would steady the realm.

sentences.zh: 君若握兵，臨大節，孰能奪之！

translations.literal: Were you to grasp military command and face great crises, who could wrest it from you!
translations.idiomatic: Were he to command armies at the crisis hour none could break him.

sentences.zh: 方今徵聘，君實宜之。

translations.literal: Just now summons and recruitment come—you truly ought to answer.
translations.idiomatic: Now recruiters knock—he ought to answer.

sentences.zh: 」於是鄉黨薦之，州郡交命，察孝廉，舉秀才、清白異行，皆不降志，世遂號之為異行。

translations.literal: " Thereupon township and village recommended him; province and commandery issued overlapping summons; he was nominated filial and incorrupt, recommended cultivated talent and pure conduct—all without bending his resolve; the age therefore styled him "extraordinary conduct."
translations.idiomatic: " Yet counties, provinces, and tribunals piled summons on him—filial, talented, pure—and he refused every title, so peers called him the man of singular principle.

sentences.zh: 元康末，潁川太守召為功曹，袞服造役之衣，杖鍤荷斧，不俟駕而行，曰：「請受下夫之役。

translations.literal: Near the end of Yuankang the governor of Yingchuan summoned him as merit clerk; Gun put on laborers' clothes, leaned on a mattock and carried an axe, set off without waiting for a carriage, saying, "Please assign me the labor of a common workman.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yuankang the Yingchuan governor wanted him as clerk of merit—Yu Gun dressed like a corvée laborer, shouldered hoe and axe, and marched without a carriage, crying, "Treat me as the lowest hireling.

sentences.zh: 」太守飾車而迎，袞逡巡辭退，請徒行入郡，將命者遂逼扶升車，納于功曹舍。

translations.literal: " The governor adorned a carriage to welcome him; Gun hesitated and withdrew, begged to walk into the commandery on foot; the commissioner then forced him into the carriage and lodged him in the merit clerk's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The governor sent a decorated rig; Yu Gun refused until handlers bundled him into the carriage and dumped him in the clerk's quarters.

sentences.zh: 既而袞自取己車而寢處焉，形雖恭而神有不可動之色。

translations.literal: Presently Gun himself fetched his own carriage and slept in it; though his bearing seemed deferential, his spirit wore an immovable color.
translations.idiomatic: He slept in his own cart anyway—demure in manner, adamant in spirit.

sentences.zh: 太守知其不屈，乃歎曰：「非常士也，吾何以降之！

translations.literal: When the governor saw he would not bend, he sighed, "This is no ordinary scholar—how am I to humble him!
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his resolve, the governor sighed that no ordinary courtesy could move him.

sentences.zh: 」厚為之禮而遣焉。

translations.literal: " He treated him lavishly and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: " He honored him richly and let him go.

sentences.zh: 齊王冏之唱義也，張泓等肆掠于陽翟，袞乃率其同族及庶姓保于禹山。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qi Sima Jiong raised the righteous cause, Zhang Hong and others ravaged Yangzhai; Gun then led his lineage kin and common clansmen to fortify Mount Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Jiong rose against usurpation and Zhang Hong looted Yangzhai, Yu Gun led clan and neighbors onto fortified Mount Yu.

sentences.zh: 是時百姓安寧，未知戰守之事，袞曰：「孔子云：'不教而戰，是謂棄之。

translations.literal: At that time the common people lived in peace and did not understand warfare or defense; Gun said, "Confucius remarked: 'To send men to battle untrained is to throw them away.'
translations.idiomatic: Peasants knew nothing of war; Yu Gun quoted Confucius—troops without training are sacrificed.

sentences.zh: '」乃集諸如士而謀曰：「二三君子相與處於險，將以安保親尊，全妻孥也。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he assembled the scholars and planned, saying, "You gentlemen dwell together in peril in order to protect parents and preserve wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: " He convened local scholars: survival together meant shielding elders and families.

sentences.zh: 古人有言：'千人聚而不以一人為主，不散則亂矣。

translations.literal: The ancients said: 'Where a thousand gather without one leader to rule them, unless they scatter they fall into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The proverb ran: a thousand men without a chief dissolve into chaos.

sentences.zh: '將若之何！

translations.literal: ' What shall we do about it!
translations.idiomatic: "What shall we do?"

sentences.zh: 」眾曰：「善。

translations.literal: " The crowd said, "Excellent.
translations.idiomatic: " The gathering shouted approval.

sentences.zh: 今日之主，非君而誰！

translations.literal: Today's leader—if not you, then who!
translations.idiomatic: "If anyone leads, it must be you."

sentences.zh: 」袞默然有間，乃言曰：「古人急病讓夷，不敢逃難，然人之立主，貴從其命也。

translations.literal: " Gun was silent a moment, then said, "The ancients yielded precedence in danger and dared not flee hardship; yet when men raise a leader they prize obedience to his commands.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu Gun paused: antiquity praised yielding rank in crisis, yet chosen leaders must still command consent.

sentences.zh: 」乃誓之曰：「無恃險，無怙亂，無暴鄰，無抽屋，無樵采人所植，無謀非德，無犯非義，戮力一心，同恤危難。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he swore them: "Do not rely on cliffs alone; do not exploit turmoil; do not abuse neighbors; do not tear down houses to strengthen ramparts; do not gather firewood others have planted; plot nothing contrary to virtue; commit nothing unjust to duty; join strength as one heart and share peril alike.
translations.idiomatic: " He administered an oath—no pillaging, no feuding with allies, share hardship together.

sentences.zh: 」眾咸從之。

translations.literal: " The multitude all assented.
translations.idiomatic: " Everyone swore the covenant.

sentences.zh: 於是峻險厄，杜蹊徑，修壁塢，樹蕃障，考功庸，計丈尺，均勞逸，通有無，繕完器備，量力任能，物應其宜，使邑推其長，裏推其賢，而身率之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they heightened perilous passes, blocked paths, repaired walled redoubts, planted barriers, assessed labor quotas, measured plots, balanced fatigue and rest, shared surplus and need, repaired weapons and gear, matched tasks to talent so goods answered needs; they had towns push forward elders and villages choose worthies, while Gun himself led.
translations.idiomatic: They walled ravines, guarded trails, tallied labor and supplies, elected hamlet heads and worthy advisers—Gun led every detail.

sentences.zh: 分數既明，號令不二，上下有禮，少長有儀，將順其美，匡救其惡。

translations.literal: Once assignments were clear and commands single, superiors and inferiors showed ritual propriety, youth and age maintained deportment; they encouraged good and amended evil.
translations.idiomatic: Orders unified; etiquette governed young and old; they amplified virtue and curbed vice.

sentences.zh: 及賊至，袞乃勒部曲，整行伍，皆持滿而勿發。

translations.literal: When bandits arrived Gun marshaled his troops and aligned ranks; every archer kept bows drawn but loosed no arrows.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders came he drew up ranks with bows taut yet silent.

sentences.zh: 賊挑戰，晏然不動，且辭焉。

translations.literal: The bandits challenged battle; he remained placidly unmoved and moreover declined.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders taunted; his lines stayed motionless and refused combat.

sentences.zh: 賊服其慎而畏其整，是以皆退，如是者三。

translations.literal: The bandits respected his caution and feared his ordered ranks; therefore they all withdrew—thus three times.
translations.idiomatic: They feared his discipline and withdrew three separate times.

sentences.zh: 時人語曰：「所謂臨事而懼、好謀而成者，其庾異行乎！」

translations.literal: Men of the time said, "What they call fearful before events yet victorious through planning—that describes Yu of singular conduct!"
translations.idiomatic: People said planning plus caution marked Yu Gun—the man called singular.

sentences.zh: 及冏歸於京師，逾年不朝，袞曰：「晉室卑矣，寇難方興！

translations.literal: When Jiong returned to the capital and longer than a year did not attend court, Gun said, "The house of Jin declines—calamity rises!
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Jiong stalled outside court Yu Gun saw Jin collapsing.

sentences.zh: 」乃攜其妻適林慮山，事其新鄉如其故鄉，言忠信，行篤敬。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he took his wife and went to Mount Linlu; he treated his new hamlet as his old hamlet, spoke loyalty and trust, acted earnest reverence.
translations.idiomatic: " He fled with his wife to Linlu peaks and honored strangers like hometown kin.

sentences.zh: 經及期年，而林慮之人歸之，咸曰庾賢。

translations.literal: After a full year passed the folk of Linlu submitted to him; all called him Worthy Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year locals called him Worthy Yu.

sentences.zh: 及石勒攻林慮，父老謀曰：「此有大頭山，九州之絕險也。

translations.literal: When Shi Le attacked Linlu the elders plotted, saying, "Here is Great Head Mountain—the extremest precipice of the nine provinces.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le struck, elders pointed to Great Head Mountain—the steepest ridge.

sentences.zh: 上有古人遺跡，可共保之。

translations.literal: Above are traces left by antiquity; together we can defend there.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient ruins crowned its crest—they could fortify there.

sentences.zh: 」惠帝遷于長安，袞乃相與登於大頭山而田於其下。

translations.literal: " When Emperor Hui moved to Chang'an, Gun together with them climbed Great Head Mountain and farmed below.
translations.idiomatic: " As Emperor Hui withdrew westward the refugee band farmed the heights.

sentences.zh: 年穀未熟，食木實，餌石蕊，同保安之，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: Before the yearly grain ripened they ate tree fruits and fed on lichenous moss; together they kept peace and harbored resolve to end their days there.
translations.idiomatic: They ate bark and moss until harvest and hoped to die untainted.

sentences.zh: 及將收穫，命子怞與之下山，中途目眩瞀，墜崖而卒。

translations.literal: When harvest neared he ordered his son You to descend the mountain with him; midway You's vision blurred and dizzy he fell from a cliff and died.
translations.idiomatic: At harvest he sent son Yu You downslope; the boy grew dizzy and plunged from the cliff.

sentences.zh: 同保赴哭曰：「天乎！

translations.literal: Those who jointly sheltered rushed to wail, saying, "Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Their coterie howled to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 獨不可舍我賢乎！

translations.literal: Could you alone not spare our worthy!"
translations.idiomatic: "Why spare everyone but our sage?"

sentences.zh: 」時人傷之曰：「庾賢絕塵避地，超然遠跡，固窮安陋，木食山棲，不與世同榮，不與人爭利，不免遭命，悲夫！」

translations.literal: People of the time mourned him with the words, "Worthy Yu shook off dust and fled the world, loftily distant from traces; steadfast in poverty, dwelling coarse in hills—eating trees and nesting hills—sharing neither worldly glory nor competing for profit; yet still fate struck—alas!"
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries lamented that Yu Gun—hermit, ascetic, harmless—still fell to cruel fate.

sentences.zh: 袞學通《詩》《書》，非法不言，非道不行，尊事耆老，惠訓蒙幼，臨人之喪必盡哀，會人之葬必躬築，勞則先之，逸則後之，言必行之，行必安之。

translations.literal: Gun thoroughly mastered the "Classic of Poetry" and "Documents"; he spoke nothing contrary to law and practiced nothing contrary to the Way; he honored elders and kindly instructed the young; encountering others' mourning he exhausted grief; joining others' burials he personally wielded the shovel—taking labor first and ease afterward; what he said he performed and what he performed he settled safely.
translations.idiomatic: He embodied Poetry and Documents—speaking only rightly, aiding funerals, elders first.

sentences.zh: 是以宗族鄉黨莫不崇仰，門人感慕，為人樹碑焉。

translations.literal: Therefore lineage and township revered him; disciples admired him and erected a stele in his honor.
translations.idiomatic: Clans idolized him; students carved him a stone.

sentences.zh: 有四子：怞、蔑、澤、捃。

translations.literal: He had four sons: You, Mie, Ze, and Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Four sons: You, Mie, Ze, Jun.

sentences.zh: 在澤生，故名澤，因捃生，故曰捃。

translations.literal: Because Ze was born at that time he received the name Ze; because Jun was born during the gleaning season he received the name Jun.
translations.idiomatic: One son arrived amid the harvest levy—names matched their births.

sentences.zh: 蔑後南渡江，中興初，為侍中。

translations.literal: Mie later crossed south of the Yangzi; at the Zhongxing restoration he became palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Mie fled south and became attendant-in-waiting after the restoration.

sentences.zh: 蔑生願，安成太守。

translations.literal: Mie begot Yuan, governor of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Mie's son Yuan governed Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 孫晷

translations.literal: Sun Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Gui

sentences.zh: 孫晷，字文度，吳國富春人，吳伏波將軍秀之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Sun Gui, courtesy name Wendu, was a man of Fuchun in the state of Wu, great-grandson of General Who Calms the Waves Sun Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Gui, styled Wendu, of Fuchun, traced descent from general Sun Xiu of Wu.

sentences.zh: 晷為兒童，未嘗被呵怒。

translations.literal: As a child he was never scolded in anger.
translations.idiomatic: Not even a harsh word marred his boyhood.

sentences.zh: 顧榮見而稱之，謂其外祖薛兼曰：「此兒神明清審，志氣貞立，非常童也。

translations.literal: Gu Rong on seeing him praised him, saying to his maternal grandfather Xue Jian, "This child's spirit is clear and his will upright—no ordinary boy.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Rong told his grandfather the boy was preternaturally steady and bright.

sentences.zh: 」及長，恭孝清約，學識有理義，每獨處幽暗之中，容止瞻望未嘗傾邪。

translations.literal: " When grown he was reverent, filial, abstemious, and principled; his learning had moral clarity; even alone in dim places his bearing and gaze never turned awry.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he was frugal, learned, and unimpeachable even in the dark.

sentences.zh: 雖侯家豐厚，而晷常布衣蔬食，躬親壟畝，誦詠不廢，欣然獨得。

translations.literal: Although his house was a marquis's plenty, Gui always wore plain cloth, ate vegetables, personally worked the fields, never ceased recitation, and joyfully found contentment alone.
translations.idiomatic: Born to wealth he chose coarse cloth, farmed his fields, and never stopped chanting texts.

sentences.zh: 父母湣其如此，欲加優饒，而夙興夜寐，無暫懈也。

translations.literal: His parents pitied him for this and wished to grant easier plenty, yet he rose early and slept late without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: Parents urged comfort but he rose before dawn and slept after dusk.

sentences.zh: 父母起居嘗饌，雖諸兄親饋，而晷不離左右。

translations.literal: When parents rose or rested at meals, though elder brothers brought dishes themselves, Gui never left their side.
translations.idiomatic: At every meal he hovered beside his parents even when brothers served.

sentences.zh: 富春車道既少，動經江川，父難於風波，每行乘籃輿，晷躬自扶侍，所詣之處，則於門外樹下籓屏之間隱息，初不令主人知之。

translations.literal: Fuchun had few roads and often required river crossings; the father dreaded waves and always rode in a sedan chair; Gui personally supported him; wherever they lodged he rested hidden between fence and trees outside the gate, never letting the host learn.
translations.idiomatic: River crossings frightened his father; Sun Gui carried his sedan and hid outside inns so hosts never fussed.

sentences.zh: 兄嘗篤疾經年，晷躬自扶侍，藥石甘苦，必經心目，跋涉山水，祈求懇至。

translations.literal: An elder brother once lay gravely ill a full year; Gui personally tended him; bitter or sweet medicine always passed his scrutiny; he crossed hills and streams beseeching gods earnestly.
translations.idiomatic: He nursed a dying brother a year—every dose tasted, every shrine visited.

sentences.zh: 而聞人之善，欣若有得；

translations.literal: When he heard others' good deeds he rejoiced as if he had gained.
translations.idiomatic: Others' virtue delighted him like personal gain.

sentences.zh: 聞人之惡，慘若有失。

translations.literal: When he heard others' faults he grieved as if he had lost.
translations.idiomatic: Others' vice saddened him like personal loss.

sentences.zh: 見人饑寒，並周贍之，鄉里贈遺，一無所受。

translations.literal: Seeing men hungry or cold he aided them together; gifts from the township he rejected entirely.
translations.idiomatic: He fed the needy and refused neighborhood gifts.

sentences.zh: 親故有窮老者數人，恆往來告索，人多厭慢之，而晷見之。

translations.literal: Several aged poor among kin and friends constantly came begging; many grew weary and rude; yet Gui treated them.
translations.idiomatic: Needy elders bored neighbors—Sun Gui welcomed them.

sentences.zh: 欣敬逾甚，寒則與同衾，食則與同器，或解衣推被以恤之。

translations.literal: With joyful reverence beyond others—cold nights shared quilts, meals shared bowls; sometimes he stripped garments or blankets to succor them.
translations.idiomatic: He shared quilts and bowls and stripped his cloak for them.

sentences.zh: 時年饑穀貴，人有生刈其稻者，晷見而避之，須去而出，既而自刈送與之。

translations.literal: In a famine year when grain was costly someone stealthily reaped his rice; Gui saw it and withdrew until they left, then himself cut grain and sent it to them.
translations.idiomatic: When thieves stole his grain he hid until they fled, then harvested rice for them.

sentences.zh: 鄉鄰感愧，莫敢侵犯。

translations.literal: Neighbors felt shame and awe and none dared trespass.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors repented and never stole again.

sentences.zh: 會稽虞喜隱居海嵎，有高世之風。

translations.literal: Yu Xi of Kuaiji dwelt hidden at the sea cliffs with lofty deportment beyond the age.
translations.idiomatic: Hermit Yu Xi of Kuaiji commanded coastal renown.

sentences.zh: 晷欽其德，聘喜弟預女為妻。

translations.literal: Gui admired his virtue and took Xi's younger brother Yu Yu's daughter as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Gui married Yu Xi's niece out of respect.

sentences.zh: 喜戒女棄華尚素，與晷同志。

translations.literal: Xi admonished his daughter to cast aside splendor for simplicity and share Gui's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi told his daughter to live plainly beside Sun Gui.

sentences.zh: 時人號為梁鴻夫婦。

translations.literal: People of the time styled them the couple of Liang Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors compared them to Liang Hong and Meng Guang.

sentences.zh: 濟陽江淳少有高操，聞晷學行過人，自東陽往候之，始面，便終日譚宴，結歡而別。

translations.literal: Jiang Chun of Jiyang in youth had lofty integrity; hearing Gui's learning surpassed others he traveled from Dongyang to wait on him; from first meeting they feasted and talked the whole day and parted bonded.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Chun traveled from Dongyang for one banquet that lasted till dusk.

sentences.zh: 司空何充為揚州，檄晷為主簿，司徒蔡謨辟為掾屬，並不就。

translations.literal: Minister of Works He Chong governed Yangzhou and summoned Gui as chief clerk; Minister over the Masses Cai Mo recruited him as staff—he accepted neither.
translations.idiomatic: He Chong and Cai Mo sought him—he refused both.

sentences.zh: 尚書經國明，州土之望，表薦晷，公車徑征。

translations.literal: The Secretariat minister eminent as the realm's pillar, hope of the soil of this province, memorialized recommending Gui; the summoning cart came directly.
translations.idiomatic: A minister of state—pillar of the province—recommended him and court coaches raced to fetch him.

sentences.zh: 會卒，時年三十八，朝野嗟痛之。

translations.literal: At that point he died at age thirty-eight; court and countryside mourned bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-eight before answering—the realm wept.

sentences.zh: 晷未及大斂，有一老父縕袍草屨，不通姓名，徑入撫柩而哭，哀聲慷慨，感於左右。

translations.literal: Before Gui received final encoffining an old man in hemp cloak and straw sandals, giving no name, entered straightway to embrace the coffin and weep; sorrowful sounds stirred all nearby.
translations.idiomatic: Before burial an unnamed elder in straw sandals rushed in and sobbed over the coffin.

sentences.zh: 哭止便出，容貌甚清，眼瞳又方，門者告之喪主，怪而追焉。

translations.literal: When weeping ceased he departed; his appearance was very pure and his pupils square; doorkeepers reported to the chief mourner who wondered and pursued.
translations.idiomatic: He vanished—features luminous, eyes square—mourners chased him.

sentences.zh: 直去不顧。

translations.literal: He walked straight away without turning.
translations.idiomatic: He strode off without looking back.

sentences.zh: 同郡顧和等百餘人歎其神貌有異，而莫之測也。

translations.literal: More than a hundred men of the commandery including Gu He sighed that his spirit visage differed yet none could fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred locals swore his face was uncanny—none understood.

sentences.zh: 顏含

translations.literal: Yan Han.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Han

sentences.zh: 顏含，字弘都，琅邪莘人也。

translations.literal: Yan Han, courtesy name Hongdu, was a native of Shen in Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Han, styled Hongdu, came from Shen in Langya.

sentences.zh: 祖欽，給事中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qin was gentleman-attendant at court.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Yan Qin served as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 父默，汝陰太守。

translations.literal: His father Mo was governor of Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: Father Yan Mo governed Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 含少有操行，以孝聞。

translations.literal: Han in youth had principled conduct and was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Young Yan Han was known for duty and devotion.

sentences.zh: 兄畿，咸寧中得疾，就醫自療，遂死於醫家。

translations.literal: His elder brother Ji during Xianning fell ill, sought a physician to treat himself, and died in the doctor's house.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Yan Ji died under a physician's care in Xianning.

sentences.zh: 家人迎喪，旐每繞樹而不可解，引喪者顛仆，稱畿言曰：「我壽命未死，但服藥太多，傷我五藏耳。

translations.literal: When the family welcomed the bier the funeral pennants wound round trees and could not be freed; pallbearers stumbled and fell; they voiced Ji's words: "My allotted span is not ended—I merely took too much medicine and injured my five viscera.
translations.idiomatic: Bearers could not move the hearse until a voice claimed Ji lived—too much medicine hurt his organs.

sentences.zh: 今當復活，慎無葬也。

translations.literal: Now I ought to revive—take care not to bury me.
translations.idiomatic: "He would revive—delay burial."

sentences.zh: 」其父祝之曰：「若爾有命復生，豈非骨肉所願！
