translations.literal: " His father prayed to him, saying, "If indeed fate restores you to life—would it not be kin's desire!
translations.idiomatic: " Father prayed that resurrection would bless the clan.

sentences.zh: 今但欲還家，不爾葬也。

translations.literal: Now we only wish you returned home—we will not bury otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: "They would bring him home unburied."

sentences.zh: 」旐乃解。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the pennants came free.
translations.idiomatic: " The catafalque loosened.

sentences.zh: 及還，其婦夢之曰：「吾當復生，可急開棺。

translations.literal: When they returned his wife dreamed him saying, "I shall revive—open the coffin swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: His wife dreamed him begging to open the coffin.

sentences.zh: 」婦頗說之。

translations.literal: " The wife largely believed it.
translations.idiomatic: She nearly believed it.

sentences.zh: 其夕，母及家人又夢之，即欲開棺，而父不聽。

translations.literal: That night mother and kin likewise dreamed so and wished to open the coffin but the father refused.
translations.idiomatic: Kin dreamed the same but the father forbade opening.

sentences.zh: 含時尚少，乃慨然曰：「非常之事，古則有之，今靈異至此，開棺之痛，孰與不開相負？

translations.literal: Han was still young and declared passionately, "Such extraordinary matters existed in antiquity; now omens reach this pitch—which pain is worse, opening or failing to open?
translations.idiomatic: Young Yan Han argued miracles demanded opening—risk matched duty.

sentences.zh: 」父母從之，乃共發棺果有生驗，以手刮棺，指爪盡傷，然氣息甚微，存亡不分矣。

translations.literal: " Parents followed him; together they opened the coffin and indeed found signs of life; he scraped the coffin with hands until nails tore away; yet breath was faint and survival uncertain.
translations.idiomatic: They opened the lid—Ji scratched weakly until nails tore—breath barely stirred.

sentences.zh: 飲哺將護，累月猶不能語，飲食所須，托之以夢。

translations.literal: Feeding and nursing many months he still could not speak; what foods he needed he conveyed through dreams.
translations.idiomatic: Months passed speechless; needs came through dreams.

sentences.zh: 闔家營視，頓廢生業，雖在母妻，不能無倦矣。

translations.literal: The whole household tended him and utterly neglected livelihood; even mothers and wives grew weary.
translations.idiomatic: Kin exhausted themselves nursing until wives grew weary.

sentences.zh: 含乃絕棄人事，躬親侍養，足不出戶者十有三年。

translations.literal: Han therefore abandoned worldly affairs and personally nursed him, not stepping outside the gate thirteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Han quit the world and nursed thirteen years indoors.

sentences.zh: 石崇重含淳行，贈以甘旨，含謝而不受。

translations.literal: Shi Chong esteemed Han's honest conduct and gifted delicacies; Han declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chong's delicacies he refused.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，答曰：「病者綿昧，生理未全，既不能進噉，又未識人惠，若當謬留，豈施者之意也！

translations.literal: Asked the reason he replied, "The sick lie dim—life principle incomplete—unable to swallow yet unaware of others' kindness—if wrongly retained would that match the donor's intent!
translations.idiomatic: He said the patient could not taste kindness—keeping gifts missed the point.

sentences.zh: 」畿竟不起。

translations.literal: " In the end Ji did not recover.
translations.idiomatic: " Brother Ji never woke.

sentences.zh: 含二親既終，兩兄繼沒，次嫂樊氏因疾失明，含課勵家人，盡心奉養，每日自嘗省藥饌，察問息耗，必簪屨束帶。

translations.literal: After both parents died and two elder brothers followed, his second sister-in-law Lady Fan went blind from illness; Han exhorted family members and devoted full care; daily he personally tasted medicines and food, examined her condition, always wearing cap and sash.
translations.idiomatic: Parents gone, brothers dead, blind sister-in-law Fan—he tasted every dose and visited formally dressed.

sentences.zh: 醫人疏方，應須髯蛇膽，而尋求備至，無由得之，含憂歎累時。

translations.literal: Physicians prescribed python gall yet despite exhaustive search none could be found; Han worried and sighed long.
translations.idiomatic: Doctors wanted python gall—none could be found.

sentences.zh: 嘗晝獨坐，忽有一青衣童子年可十三四，持一青囊授含，含開視，乃蛇膽也。

translations.literal: Once sitting alone by day he suddenly saw a blue-robed boy about thirteen or fourteen bearing a blue pouch; handing it to Han, Han opened it and found snake gall.
translations.idiomatic: A boy in blue left a pouch—inside lay snake gall.

sentences.zh: 童子逡巡出戶，化成青鳥飛去。

translations.literal: The boy hesitated out the door, transformed into a blue bird and flew away.
translations.idiomatic: The messenger became a bluebird and flew off.

sentences.zh: 得膽，藥成，嫂病即愈。

translations.literal: With the gall the medicine succeeded and the sister-in-law's illness healed.
translations.idiomatic: The medicine cured her blindness.

sentences.zh: 由是著名。

translations.literal: From this he became celebrated.
translations.idiomatic: His fame spread.

sentences.zh: 本州辟，不就。

translations.literal: The province summoned him; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He refused provincial summons.

sentences.zh: 東海王越以為太傅參軍，出補闓陽令。

translations.literal: Prince of Donghai Sima Yue appointed him secretary on the grand tutor's staff and sent him out as magistrate of Kaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai, named him tutor's secretary and Kaiyang magistrate.

sentences.zh: 元帝初鎮下邳，復命為參軍。

translations.literal: When Yuan-di first quartered at Xiapi he again ordered him aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan-di camped at Xiapi Yan Han joined staff again.

sentences.zh: 過江，以含為上虞令。

translations.literal: After crossing the Yangzi he appointed Han magistrate of Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river he governed Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 轉王國郎中、丞相東閣祭酒，出為東陽太守。

translations.literal: He transferred to gentleman-of-the-household for princely establishments, libationer of the Eastern Pavilion for the chief minister, then went out as governor of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to prince's secretary, eastern pavilion libationer, then Dongyang governor.

sentences.zh: 東宮初建，含以儒素篤行補太子中庶子，遷黃門侍郎、本州大中正，曆散騎常侍、大司農。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Palace was first founded Han was supplementary attendant for the heir apparent for learned purity and honest conduct; he advanced to palace attendant and chief rectifier of his native province, passing through supernumerary gentleman attendant and minister of agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Named tutor to the crown prince for his scholar's honesty, he climbed to palace cadre, provincial classifier, chamberlain, and minister of finance.

sentences.zh: 豫討蘇峻功，封西平縣侯，拜侍中，除吳郡太守。

translations.literal: For merit in the advance against Su Jun he was enfeoffed marquis of Xiping county, appointed palace attendant, then designated governor of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His role against Su Jun earned the Xiping marquisate, court attendantship, then Wu governorship.

sentences.zh: 王導問含曰：「卿今蒞名郡，政將何先？

translations.literal: Wang Dao asked Han, "Now that you govern a famed commandery—what comes first in administration?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao asked his priorities atop Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「王師歲動，編戶虛耗，南北權豪競招游食，國弊家豐，執事之憂。

translations.literal: " He answered, "Imperial armies campaign yearly; registered households waste away; northern and southern magnates vie to harbor wandering dependents—the state grows poor while houses grow rich; this is what burdens officials.
translations.idiomatic: "He cited armies draining taxpayers while magnates hoarded clients—the ruler's headache.

sentences.zh: 且當征之勢門，使反田桑，數年之間，欲令戶給人足，如其禮樂，俟之明宰。

translations.literal: One must summon such powerful gates and return them to farming and silkworms; within several years wish to make households sufficient and men fed—rites and music may await a brighter governor.
translations.idiomatic: "Drive parasites back to the soil; prosperity precedes ritual reform.

sentences.zh: 」含所曆簡而有恩，明而能斷，然以威禦下。

translations.literal: " Where Han governed he was concise yet merciful, perspicacious yet decisive, yet employed awe to control subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: "He ruled Wu with terse mercy, sharp judgment, and stern discipline.

sentences.zh: 導歎曰：「顏公在事，吳人斂手矣。

translations.literal: Dao sighed, "When Lord Yan holds office the people of Wu fold their hands.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao said Wu folk would fear to stir under Yan Han.

sentences.zh: 」未之官，復為侍中。

translations.literal: " Before he reached office he again became palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: "Recall reached him before he took his Wu seat.

sentences.zh: 尋除國子祭酒，加散騎常侍，遷光祿勳，以年老遜位。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed libationer of the imperial academy, added supernumerary gentleman attendant, promoted minister of the imperial household, and owing to age yielded office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to academy libationer and chamberlain, then retired with age.

sentences.zh: 成帝美其素行，就加右光祿大夫，門施行馬，賜床帳被褥，敕太官四時致膳，固辭不受。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng praised his plain conduct and additionally conferred right grand counselor for splendid virtue, ordered gateposts for his carriage lane, gifted bedding and curtains, commanded the palace kitchen to supply seasonal fare—he firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng piled honors—carriage posts, quilts, royal kitchens—all refused.

sentences.zh: 于時論者以王導帝之師傅，名位隆重，百僚宜為降禮。

translations.literal: At that time debaters held that Wang Dao as the emperor's tutor enjoyed lofty name and rank—every official ought to bow lower.
translations.idiomatic: Critics wanted officials to grovel because Wang Dao taught the throne.

sentences.zh: 太常馮懷以問於含，含曰：「王公雖重，理無偏敬，降禮之言，或是諸君事宜。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Ceremonies Feng Huai asked Han; Han said, "Though the lord duke is weighty, principle knows no partial reverence; talk of lowering bows perhaps suits you gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Han told Feng Huai that protocol owed Wang Dao no special bow.

sentences.zh: 鄙人老矣，不識時務。

translations.literal: This rustic is old and does not grasp current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: "This old man ignores fashion."

sentences.zh: 」既而告人曰：「吾聞伐國不問仁人。

translations.literal: " Then he told others, "I have heard one does not ask humane men about attacking states.
translations.idiomatic: "He muttered that tacticians should not quiz sages about invasion.

sentences.zh: 向馮祖思問佞於我，我有邪德乎？

translations.literal: Just now Feng Zusi asked flattery of me—do I harbor wicked virtue?
translations.idiomatic: "Feng had tried to bait him into servility."

sentences.zh: 」人嘗論少正卯、盜蹠其惡孰深。

translations.literal: " Men once debated whether Shaozheng Mao or Robber Zhi acted worse.
translations.idiomatic: "Someone compared Shaozheng Mao to Robber Zhi.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「正卯雖奸，不至剖人棄膳，盜蹠為甚。

translations.literal: Someone said, "Though Mao was treacherous he never carved men or threw away meals—Zhi was worse.
translations.idiomatic: "One argued Zhi's violence exceeded Mao's.

sentences.zh: 」含曰：「為惡彰露，人思加戮；

translations.literal: " Han said, "When evil lies exposed men wish to add punishment;
translations.idiomatic: "Yan Han countered that open vice invites punishment;

sentences.zh: 隱伏之奸，非聖不誅。

translations.literal: hidden treachery—unless a sage strikes it down—survives.
translations.idiomatic: hidden malice kills unless sages expose it.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，少正為甚。

translations.literal: By this reasoning Mao was worse.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Mao was deadlier.

sentences.zh: 」眾咸服焉。

translations.literal: " The crowd all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: "The hall agreed.

sentences.zh: 郭璞嘗遇含，欲為之筮。

translations.literal: Guo Pu once met Han and wished to cast milfoil for him.
translations.idiomatic: Diviner Guo Pu offered him a reading.

sentences.zh: 含曰：「年在天，位在人，修己而天不與者，命也；

translations.literal: Han said, "Years lie with Heaven, positions with men; cultivate oneself yet Heaven does not aid—that is fate;
translations.idiomatic: "Years belong to fate; effort defines character;

sentences.zh: 守道而人不知者，性也。

translations.literal: guard the Way yet men do not understand—that is nature.
translations.idiomatic: integrity needs no oracle.

sentences.zh: 自有性命，無勞蓍龜。

translations.literal: Life and nature exist of themselves—no need to trouble yarrow tortoise.
translations.idiomatic: "Life answers itself—skip the shells."

sentences.zh: 」桓溫求婚於含，含以其盛滿，不許。

translations.literal: " Huan Wen sought marriage with Han; Han refused because Wen had grown too full of himself.
translations.idiomatic: He spurned Huan Wen's match as hubris.

sentences.zh: 惟與鄧攸深交。

translations.literal: He associated deeply only with Deng You.
translations.idiomatic: Only Deng You won his trust.

sentences.zh: 或問江左群士優劣，答曰：「周伯仁之正，鄧伯道之清，卞望之之節，餘則吾不知也。

translations.literal: Asked to rank eastern Jin gentlemen he replied, "Zhou Bor'en's rectitude, Deng Bodao's purity, Bian Wangzhi's integrity—for the rest I know nothing.
translations.idiomatic: "He praised Zhou, Deng, and Bian—and dismissed the rest.

sentences.zh: 」其雅重行實，抑絕浮偽如此。

translations.literal: " Thus he esteemed solid conduct and suppressed hollow pretense.
translations.idiomatic: "So he weighed deeds over fame.

sentences.zh: 致仕二十餘年，年九十三卒。

translations.literal: More than twenty years in retirement he died at ninety-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at ninety-three after twenty quiet years.

sentences.zh: 遺命素棺薄斂。

translations.literal: His testament ordered plain coffin and thin burial.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a plain coffin.

sentences.zh: 諡曰靖。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Canonized as Jing.

sentences.zh: 喪在殯而鄰家失火，移棺紼斷，火將至而滅，僉以為淳誠所感也。

translations.literal: While the bier still awaited burial a neighbor's fire broke out; moving the coffin the ropes snapped; flames approached yet died—all deemed it moved by pure sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral flames reversed—people called it heaven's nod to his virtue.

sentences.zh: 三子：髦、謙、約。

translations.literal: Three sons: Mao, Qian, Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Three sons—Mao, Qian, and Yue—carried the line.

sentences.zh: 髦曆黃門郎、侍中、光祿勳，謙至安成太守，約零陵太守，並有聲譽。

translations.literal: Mao rose through palace attendant and chamberlain; Qian reached governor of Ancheng; Yue governed Lingling—all enjoyed reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Each son earned office and renown.

sentences.zh: 劉殷

translations.literal: Liu Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin

sentences.zh: 劉殷，字長盛，新興人也。

translations.literal: Liu Yin, courtesy name Changsheng, was a native of Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin, styled Changsheng, hailed from Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 高祖陵，漢光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His eminent ancestor Ling served Han as palace counselor for splendid virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestor Liu Ling had been Han counselor of splendid virtue.

sentences.zh: 殷七歲喪父，哀毀過禮，服喪三年，未曾見齒。

translations.literal: At seven Yin lost his father; grief wasted him beyond ritual propriety; mourning three years he never showed teeth in smile.
translations.idiomatic: Fatherless at seven he mourned beyond measure—three years without a smile.

sentences.zh: 曾祖母王氏，盛冬思堇而不言，食不飽者一旬矣。

translations.literal: His great-grandmother Lady Wang in deepest winter longed for shepherd's purse yet spoke not; she had eaten without fullness ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandmother Wang craved winter greens yet starved in silence.

sentences.zh: 殷怪而問之，王言其故。

translations.literal: Yin wondered and questioned her; Wang explained the cause.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed until she admitted hunger.

sentences.zh: 殷時年九歲，乃於澤中慟哭，曰：「殷罪釁深重，幼丁艱罰，王母在堂，無旬月之養。

translations.literal: Yin was nine years old; therefore he wailed in the marsh, saying, "Yin's guilt runs deep; suffering punishments young, the royal grandmother remains in hall yet lacks even ten days' support.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he keened in the marsh over failing her.

sentences.zh: 殷為人子，而所思無獲，皇天后土，願垂哀湣。

translations.literal: Yin as a son cannot obtain what she longs for—may Heaven and Earth pity.
translations.idiomatic: "He begged heaven for greens.

sentences.zh: 」聲不絕者半日，於是忽若有人云：「止，止聲。

translations.literal: " His voice did not cease half a day; then suddenly someone seemed to say, "Stop—stop the sound.
translations.idiomatic: "A voice hushed him halfway through the day.

sentences.zh: 」殷收淚視地，便有堇生焉，因得斛餘而歸，食而不減，至時，堇生乃盡。

translations.literal: " Yin dried tears and looked at the ground—shepherd's purse sprouted forth; he gathered more than a hu and returned; eating it did not diminish until season's end when growth ceased.
translations.idiomatic: "Winter weeds burst from the mud—enough to feed her for the season.

sentences.zh: 又嘗夜夢人謂之曰：「西籬下有粟。

translations.literal: Again he once dreamed someone told him, "West of the fence lies millet.
translations.idiomatic: A dream pointed west of the fence.

sentences.zh: 」寤而掘之，得粟十五鐘，銘曰「七年粟百石，以賜孝子劉殷。

translations.literal: " Awakening he dug and obtained fifteen zhong of grain whose inscription read "Seven-year grain one hundred shi—to grant the filial son Liu Yin.
translations.idiomatic: "He unearthed inscribed grain vaults meant for him.

sentences.zh: 」自是食之，七載方盡。

translations.literal: " From then he ate it—seven years elapsed before it ended.
translations.idiomatic: "The grain lasted seven years.

sentences.zh: 時人嘉其至性通感，競以穀帛遺之。

translations.literal: People of the time praised his utmost nature resonating with spirits and strove to gift grain and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors flooded him with grain and cloth.

sentences.zh: 殷受而不謝，直-{云}-待後貴當相酬耳。

translations.literal: Yin accepted without thanks and simply stated he would repay when later honored.
translations.idiomatic: He took gifts promising repayment after fortune rose.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，博通經史，綜核羣言，文章詩賦靡不該覽，性倜儻，有濟世之志，儉而不陋，清而不介，望之頹然而不可侵也。

translations.literal: At the capping age he mastered classics and histories, summarized myriad doctrines, essays and rhapsodies none omitted; nature was magnanimous with ambition to aid the age—frugal yet not coarse, pure yet not stiff—looking weary yet inviolable.
translations.idiomatic: Capped, he commanded every classic—bold, austere, formidable.

sentences.zh: 鄉黨親族莫不稱之。

translations.literal: Townsmen and kin alike praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Kin and neighbors praised him.

sentences.zh: 郡命主簿，州辟從事，皆以供養無主，辭不赴命。

translations.literal: The commandery appointed chief clerk; the province summoned aide—both he declined citing no one to support kin.
translations.idiomatic: He refused clerkships to nurse kin.

sentences.zh: 司空、齊王攸辟為掾，征南將軍羊祜召參軍事，皆以疾辭。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Prince of Qi Sima You summoned him as aide; General Who Conquers the South Yang Hu called him to military staff—both pleas he declined citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: He spurned Sima You and Yang Hu.

sentences.zh: 同郡張宣子，識達之士也，勸殷就徵。

translations.literal: Fellow townsman Zhang Xuanzi, a perspicacious gentleman, urged Yin to answer summons.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuanzi urged him to serve.

sentences.zh: 殷曰：「當今二公，有晉之棟楹也。

translations.literal: Yin said, "The two lords today are Jin's pillars and ridgepoles.
translations.idiomatic: "Those grandees are palace pillars.

sentences.zh: 吾方希達如榱椽耳，不憑之，豈能立乎！

translations.literal: I merely hope to rise like rafters—without leaning on them how stand?
translations.idiomatic: "He compared himself to roof beams needing timber.

sentences.zh: 吾今王母在堂，既應他命，無容不竭盡臣禮，使不得就養。

translations.literal: Now my royal grandmother remains in hall; once accepting another summons I cannot exhaust minister duty while failing to nourish her.
translations.idiomatic: "Grandmother still lived—office would steal her care.

sentences.zh: 子輿所以辭齊大夫，良以色養無主故耳。

translations.literal: This is why Ziyu declined the Qi grandee—because tender nurture lacked a guardian.
translations.idiomatic: "Like Zengzi's excuse—care came first.

sentences.zh: 」宣子曰：「如子所言，豈庸人所識哉！

translations.literal: " Xuanzi said, "According to your words—how could vulgar men understand!
translations.idiomatic: "Zhang swore few could grasp him.

sentences.zh: 而今而後，吾子當為吾師矣。

translations.literal: Henceforth you must be my teacher.
translations.idiomatic: "He vowed to learn from Liu Yin.

sentences.zh: 」遂以女妻之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he gave his daughter as wife.
translations.idiomatic: "He married Liu Yin his daughter.

sentences.zh: 宣子者，并州豪族也，家富於財，其妻怒曰：「我女年始十四。

translations.literal: Xuanzi belonged to Bingzhou's powerful clan; his household overflowed with wealth; his wife angrily said, "My daughter is only fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: His wife raged—why wed a girl of fourteen to Liu?

sentences.zh: 姿識如此，何慮不得為公侯妃，而遽以妻劉殷乎！

translations.literal: With such grace and insight why fear becoming a lord's consort—yet hastily marry her to Liu Yin!
translations.idiomatic: "She deserved princes—not a rustic scholar.

sentences.zh: 」宣子曰：「非爾所及也。

translations.literal: " Xuanzi said, "That lies beyond you.
translations.idiomatic: "Zhang said she misunderstood.

sentences.zh: 」誡其女曰：「劉殷至孝冥感，兼才識超世，此人終當遠達，為世名公，汝其謹事之。

translations.literal: " He admonished his daughter, "Liu Yin's utmost filial piety moves spirits and combines talents surpassing the age—this man will surely rise far and become a famed lord of the generation—you must serve him carefully.
translations.idiomatic: "He praised Liu Yin's destiny.

sentences.zh: 」張氏性亦婉順，事王母以孝聞，奉殷如君父焉。

translations.literal: " Lady Zhang likewise gentle obeyed; serving the royal grandmother with filial fame she honored Yin like lord and father.
translations.idiomatic: "His bride served grandmother like kin.

sentences.zh: 及王氏卒，殷夫婦毀瘠，幾至滅性，時柩在殯而西鄰失火，風勢甚盛，殷夫婦叩殯號哭，火遂越燒東家。

translations.literal: When Wang died Yin and wife wasted away nearly destroying themselves; while the bier yet awaited burial western neighbors caught fire; winds fierce—Yin couple knocked the bier wailing—fire leapt past to burn eastern houses.
translations.idiomatic: Their mourning shifted a blaze away from the coffin.

sentences.zh: 後有二白鳩巢其庭樹，自是名譽彌顯。

translations.literal: Afterward two white doves nested in their courtyard tree—from this reputation grew brighter.
translations.idiomatic: White doves nested—his fame soared.

sentences.zh: 太傅楊駿輔政，備禮聘殷，殷以母老固辭。

translations.literal: Grand tutor Yang Jun dominated court and summoned Yin with full ritual; Yin firmly declined citing aged mother.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun courted him—he cited mother.

sentences.zh: 駿於是表之，優詔遂其高志，聽終色養，敕所在供其衣食，蠲其徭賦，賜帛二百匹，穀五百斛。

translations.literal: Jun therefore memorialized; gracious edict fulfilled his lofty intent, permitted lifelong tender nurture, commanded localities supply clothing and food, remit labor dues, grant two hundred bolts silk, five hundred hu grain.
translations.idiomatic: The court fed mother and son and waived taxes.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫纂位，孫秀重殷名，以散騎常侍徵之，殷逃奔雁門。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao usurped the throne; Sun Xi prized Yin's name and summoned him supernumerary gentleman attendant—Yin fled to Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: He fled Sun Xi's summons under Sima Lun.

sentences.zh: 及齊王冏輔政，辟為大司馬軍諮祭酒。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qi Sima Jiong assisted government he recruited Yin as libationer for grand marshal army consultations.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jiong named him war council libationer.

sentences.zh: 既至，謂殷曰；

translations.literal: Once arrived he addressed Yin;
translations.idiomatic: At audience Sima Jiong challenged him:

sentences.zh: 「先王虛心召君，君不至。

translations.literal: "The former king summoned you with humble heart—you did not come.
translations.idiomatic: "Prior prince called—why ignore?

sentences.zh: 今孤辟君，君何能屈也？

translations.literal: Now this orphan summons you—how can you humble yourself?
translations.idiomatic: "Why obey now?

sentences.zh: 」殷曰：「世祖以大聖應期，先王以至德輔世，既堯舜為君，稷契為佐，故殷希以一夫而距千乘，為不可回之圖，幸邀唐虞之世，是以不懼斧鉞之戮耳。

translations.literal: " Yin said, "Shizu matched the great sage's age; the former king aided the age with utmost virtue—already Yao-Shun served as rulers, Ji-Xie as assistants—therefore Yin hoped one common man might refuse a thousand chariots as immovable plan, fortunate to inhabit Tang-Yu ages—thus feared no axe.
translations.idiomatic: "He compared prior refusal to mythic purity.

sentences.zh: 今殿下以神武睿姿，除殘反政，然聖跡稍粗，嚴威滋肅，殷若復爾，恐招華士之誅，故不敢不至也。

translations.literal: Now Your Highness with divine martial sagacity removes cruelty and restores rule—yet sacred traces turn coarse and stern awe spreads—if Yin acted again would fear Huashi's execution—therefore dared not refuse to attend.
translations.idiomatic: "Now tyrants punish dissent—so he came.

sentences.zh: 」冏奇之，轉拜新興太守，明刑旌善，甚有政能。

translations.literal: " Jiong marveled and transferred him governor of Xinxing—clarifying punishments and honoring goodness—very capable.
translations.idiomatic: "Sima Jiong made him Xinxing governor.

sentences.zh: 屬永嘉之亂，沒于劉聰。

translations.literal: When Yongjia turmoil struck he fell captive to Liu Cong.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongjia disaster delivered him to Liu Cong.

sentences.zh: 聰奇其才而擢任之，累至侍中、太保、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Cong admired his talent and promoted him cumulatively to palace attendant, grand guardian, and recorder of secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong raised him to chief minister ranks.

sentences.zh: 殷恆戒子孫曰：「事君之法，當務幾諫，凡人尚不可面斥其過，而況萬乘乎！

translations.literal: Yin constantly warned sons and grandsons, "Serving lords requires subtle remonstrance—ordinary men should not rebuke face to face—how much less the Son of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: He taught heirs to counsel rulers gently.

sentences.zh: 夫犯顏之禍，將彰君過，宜上思召公咨商之義，下念鮑勳觸鱗之誅也。

translations.literal: The peril of offending dignity will expose the ruler's faults—ponder Duke Shao's consultative duty above and Bao Xun's touching scales execution below.
translations.idiomatic: "Remonstrate like Duke Shao—not rash like Bao Xun.

sentences.zh: 」在聰之朝，與公卿恂恂然，常有後己之色。

translations.literal: " At Cong's court he stood deferential among dukes—often yielding place.
translations.idiomatic: "At Han Zhao court he stayed humble.

sentences.zh: 士不修操行者，無得入其門，然滯理不申，藉殷而濟者，亦已百數。

translations.literal: Scholars lacking conduct might not enter his gate—yet stalled lawsuits relying on Yin for rescue numbered over a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He barred poseurs yet aided countless plaintiffs.

sentences.zh: 有七子，五子各授一經。

translations.literal: He had seven sons—five each studied one classic.
translations.idiomatic: Seven sons studied classics.

sentences.zh: 一子授《太史公》，一子授《漢書》，一門之內，七業俱興，北州之學，殷門為盛。

translations.literal: One son studied "Grand Scribe Records"; another "Han History"—within one gate seven pursuits flourished—northern provinces counted Yin's school foremost.
translations.idiomatic: His school dominated northern letters.

sentences.zh: 竟以壽終。

translations.literal: He ended life by natural death.
translations.idiomatic: He died full of years.

sentences.zh: 王延

translations.literal: Wang Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan

sentences.zh: 王延，字延元。

translations.literal: Wang Yan, courtesy name Yanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan, styled Yanyuan.

sentences.zh: 西河人也。

translations.literal: He was a man of Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: He came from Xihe.

sentences.zh: 九歲喪母，泣血三年，幾至滅性。

translations.literal: At nine he lost his mother; weeping blood three years he nearly destroyed his nature.
translations.idiomatic: Motherless at nine he mourned bloodily.

sentences.zh: 每至忌日，則悲啼至旬。

translations.literal: Each memorial day he mourned aloud near a fortnight.
translations.idiomatic: Anniversaries brought weeks of tears.

sentences.zh: 繼母卜氏遇之無道，恆以薄穰及敗麻頭與延貯衣。

translations.literal: Stepmother Lady Bu treated him cruelly—always stuffing his clothes with husks and frayed hemp heads.
translations.idiomatic: Stepmother stuffed his quilts with chaff.

sentences.zh: 其姑聞而問之，延知而不言，事母彌謹。

translations.literal: His aunt heard and questioned him; Yan knew yet spoke not—serving mother grew ever careful.
translations.idiomatic: He hid her cruelty and grew more dutiful.

sentences.zh: 卜氏嘗盛冬思生魚，敕延求而不獲，杖之流血。

translations.literal: Lady Bu once in deep winter craved fresh fish—ordered Yan to seek yet could not obtain—beat him till blood flowed.
translations.idiomatic: She beat him bloody failing to fetch winter fish.

sentences.zh: 延尋汾叩淩而哭，忽有一魚長五尺，踴出水上，延取以進母。

translations.literal: Yan traced the Fen beating ice and weeping—suddenly a fish five chi long leaped from the water; Yan took it to present mother.
translations.idiomatic: He cracked river ice until a giant fish leaped forth.

sentences.zh: 卜氏食之，積日不盡，於是心悟，撫延如己生。

translations.literal: Lady Bu ate it days without finishing—thereupon her heart awakened and she cherished Yan like a born son.
translations.idiomatic: The miracle thawed her heart.

sentences.zh: 延事親色養，夏則扇枕席，冬則以身溫被，隆立盛寒，體無全衣，而親極滋味。

translations.literal: Yan served parents with joyful nurture—summer fanning pillows and mats—winter warming quilts with his body—standing frozen yet kin tasted finest flavors.
translations.idiomatic: He fanned beds in summer, warmed quilts in winter—parents ate best while he froze.

sentences.zh: 晝則傭賃，夜則誦書，遂究覽經史，皆通大義。

translations.literal: By day he hired out labor; by night recited texts—thereupon thoroughly perused classics and histories—all grasped great meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Days laboring, nights reading—he mastered the canon.

sentences.zh: 州郡禮辟，貪供養不起。

translations.literal: Commandery and prefecture summoned him with ritual courtesy—greedy to stay home and nurture kin he did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: He refused honors to keep nursing parents.

sentences.zh: 父母終後，廬於墓側，非其蠶不衣，非其耕不食。

translations.literal: After parents died he hutched beside tombs—wore only silk he reaped and ate only grain he ploughed.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned at the graves wearing only homespun from his silkworms.

sentences.zh: 屬天下喪亂，隨劉元海遷于平陽，農蠶之暇，訓誘宗族，侃侃不倦。

translations.literal: When the realm collapsed in chaos he followed Liu Yuanhai moving to Pingyang; between farming and silk work he instructed lineage kin tirelessly.
translations.idiomatic: Amid turmoil he followed Liu Yuan to Pingyang and taught kin between furrows.

sentences.zh: 家牛一生犢，他人認之，延牽而授與，初無吝色。

translations.literal: Household cattle once calved—another claimed the calf; Yan led it over and handed it without stinginess.
translations.idiomatic: He gave away a disputed calf without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 其人後自知妄認，送犢還延，叩頭謝罪，延仍以與之，不復取也。

translations.literal: The man later knew his claim false—returned the calf apologizing—Yan still gave it back and took nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Even after restitution he let the neighbor keep the calf.

sentences.zh: 年六十，方仕于劉聰，稍遷尚書左丞，至金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At sixty he first served Liu Cong—advanced gradually to vice-president of the left secretariat and reached grand counselor for splendid golden purple.
translations.idiomatic: At sixty he entered Liu Cong's service and rose to chief minister rank.

sentences.zh: 聰死後，靳準將作亂，謀之於延，延不從。

translations.literal: After Cong died Jin Zhun plotted rebellion—consulted Yan—Yan refused.
translations.idiomatic: He spurned Jin Zhun's coup plot.

sentences.zh: 准既誅劉氏，自號漢天王，以延為左光祿大夫，延又大罵不受，准遂殺之。

translations.literal: Once Zhun slaughtered the Liu clan he styled himself Heaven-King of Han—appointed Yan left grand counselor for splendid virtue—Yan cursed and refused—Zhun killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun murdered the imperial clan and offered Yan high office—Yan cursed him and died for it.

sentences.zh: 王談

translations.literal: Wang Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tan

sentences.zh: 王談，吳興烏程人也。

translations.literal: Wang Tan was a man of Wucheng in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tan came from Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 年十歲，父為鄰人竇度所殺。

translations.literal: At ten years old his father was murdered by neighbor Dou Du.
translations.idiomatic: His father fell to neighbor Dou Du when Wang Tan was ten.

sentences.zh: 談陰有復仇志，而懼為度所疑，寸刃不畜，日夜伺度，未得。

translations.literal: Tan secretly harbored revenge yet feared Dou's suspicion—kept no blade—day and night watched Dou without chance.
translations.idiomatic: He hid his vendetta and stalked Dou Du weaponless.

sentences.zh: 至年十八，乃密市利鍤，陽若耕鋤者。

translations.literal: At eighteen he secretly bought sharp spades pretending to farm.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he hid iron spades under farm tools.

sentences.zh: 度常乘船出入，經一橋下，談伺度行還，伏草中，度既過，談於橋上以鍤斬之，應手而死。

translations.literal: Dou often boated beneath a bridge—Tan waited till Dou returned—hid in grass—once Dou passed Tan struck him atop the bridge—he died instantly.
translations.idiomatic: He ambushed Dou beneath the bridge and killed him with a spade.

sentences.zh: 既而歸罪有司，太守孔岩義其孝勇，列上宥之。

translations.literal: Then he surrendered to authorities—Prefect Kong Yan honored filial valor and memorialized pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Kong Yan pardoned him for righteous revenge.

sentences.zh: 岩諸子為孫恩所害，無嗣，談乃移居會稽，修理岩父子墳墓，盡其心力。

translations.literal: Yan's sons died at Sun En's hands leaving no heirs—Tan moved to Kuaiji tending Yan's graves with utmost heart.
translations.idiomatic: He tended patron Kong Yan's tomb after Sun En slew Kong's sons.

sentences.zh: 後太守孔廞究其義行，元興三年，舉談為孝廉，時稱其得人。

translations.literal: Later Prefect Kong Yin investigated his righteousness—in Yuanxing third year nominated Tan filial and honest—people praised the choice.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Kong Yin cited him as filial exemplar.

sentences.zh: 談不應召，終於家。

translations.literal: Tan did not answer summons—ended life at home.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed home until death.

sentences.zh: 桑虞

translations.literal: Sang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Yu

sentences.zh: 桑虞，字子深，魏郡黎陽人也。

translations.literal: Sang Yu, courtesy name Zishen, was a native of Liyang in Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Yu, styled Zishen, hailed from Liyang.

sentences.zh: 父沖，有深識遠量，惠帝時為黃門郎。

translations.literal: His father Chong possessed deep insight and distant judgment—during Emperor Hui served as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Father Sang Chong served at court with foresight.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒執權，引為司馬。

translations.literal: Prince of Hejian Sima Yong wielded power—summoned Chong as marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong named Chong marshal.

sentences.zh: 沖知顒必敗，就職一旬，便稱疾求退。

translations.literal: Chong knew Yong must fall—after ten days on duty feigned illness seeking retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Chong quit Yong's staff within ten days.

sentences.zh: 虞仁孝自天至，年十四喪父，毀瘠過禮，日以米百粒用糝藜藿，其姊諭之曰：「汝毀瘠如此，必至滅性，滅性不孝，宜自抑割。

translations.literal: Yu was humane and filial from Heaven—at fourteen when father died grief wasted him beyond ritual—daily sprinkled a hundred grains of rice into weed porridge—his elder sister advised, "Such wasting must destroy nature—to destroy nature is unfilial—curb yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at fourteen he starved himself until his sister pleaded moderation.

sentences.zh: 」虞曰：「藜藿雜米，足以勝哀。

translations.literal: " Yu said, "Weeds mixed with rice suffice to bear grief.
translations.idiomatic: "He insisted weeds and rice honored grief enough.

sentences.zh: 」虞有園在宅北數里，瓜果初熟，有人逾垣盜之。

translations.literal: " Yu held an orchard several li north of home—melons first ripening—someone vaulted the wall stealing.
translations.idiomatic: "Thieves stole melons from his orchard.

sentences.zh: 虞以園援多棘刺，恐偷見人驚走而致傷損，乃使奴為之開道。

translations.literal: Yu thought thorns dense round the garden—feared thief seeing people would bolt and harm himself—ordered slaves clear a path.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared thorns so thieves would not hurt themselves fleeing.

sentences.zh: 及偷負瓜將出，見道通利，知虞使除之，乃送所盜瓜，叩頭請罪。

translations.literal: When thief bore melons out seeing easy road knew Yu cleared it—returned stolen melons knocked heads begging forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Thieves returned fruit ashamed.

sentences.zh: 虞乃歡然，盡以瓜與之。

translations.literal: Yu cheerfully gave them all melons.
translations.idiomatic: He gifted every melon.

sentences.zh: 嘗行，寄宿逆旅，同宿客失脯，疑虞為盜。

translations.literal: Once traveling lodging at inn fellow lodger lost dried meat suspecting Yu thief.
translations.idiomatic: An innmate blamed him for stolen jerky.

sentences.zh: 虞默然無言，便解衣償之。

translations.literal: Yu silent stripped clothes compensating.
translations.idiomatic: He paid with his coat in silence.

sentences.zh: 主人曰：「此舍數失魚肉雞鴨，多是狐狸偷去，君何以疑人？

translations.literal: Host said, "This inn often loses fish meat poultry—mostly foxes stealing—why suspect men?
translations.idiomatic: The landlord blamed foxes—not Sang Yu.

sentences.zh: 」乃將脯主至山塚間尋求，果得之。

translations.literal: " Led jerky owner among hill tombs seeking—indeed found them.
translations.idiomatic: "They recovered meat near graves.

sentences.zh: 客求還衣，虞投之不顧。

translations.literal: Guest begged clothes back—Yu tossed aside ignoring.
translations.idiomatic: He refused his cloak back.

sentences.zh: 虞諸兄仕于石勒之世，咸登顯位，惟虞恥臣非類，陰欲避地海東，會丁母憂，遂止。

translations.literal: Yu's brothers served Shi Le's court—all rose high—only Yu ashamed serving aliens secretly wished flee east across sea—when mother died mourning halted plan.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers served Later Zhao—he refused alien masters until mourning trapped him.

sentences.zh: 哀毀骨立，廬於墓側。

translations.literal: Grief wasted him skeletal—hutched tomb side.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned beside mother's grave.

sentences.zh: 五年後，石勒以為武城令。

translations.literal: Five years later Shi Le appointed him magistrate of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le named him Wucheng magistrate.

sentences.zh: 虞以密邇黃河，去海微近，將申前志，欣然就職。

translations.literal: Yu because close to Yellow River near sea could fulfill former intent—accepted gladly.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal post suited his escape plan.

sentences.zh: 石季龍太守劉徵甚器重之，徵遷青州刺史，請虞長史，帶祝阿郡。

translations.literal: Shi Jilong's prefect Liu Zheng esteemed him—when Zheng promoted Qingzhou prefect summoned Yu senior clerk heading Zhu'a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Liu Zheng made him aide.

sentences.zh: 徵遇疾還鄴，令虞監行州府屬。

translations.literal: Zheng fell ill returning Ye ordered Yu supervise prefectural offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu fell ill Sang Yu ran the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 季龍死，國中大亂，朝廷以虞名父之子，必能立功海岱，潛遣東莞人華挺授虞甯朔將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: When Jilong died chaos engulfed the state—court thought Yu famous father's son—surely able to achieve merit on coast and Taishan—secretly sent Dongguan man Hua Ting appointing Yu general Who Pacifies the North and Qingzhou inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao chaos brought recruiters offering Qingzhou—Sang Yu refused glory.

sentences.zh: 虞曰：「功名非吾志也。

translations.literal: Yu said, "Merit and fame are not my aspiration.
translations.idiomatic: "He said rank meant nothing.

sentences.zh: 」乃附使者啟，讓刺史，靖居海右，不交境外。

translations.literal: " Therefore attached petition yielding inspector—peacefully dwelling seaward—no dealings beyond borders.
translations.idiomatic: "He stayed coastal and cut ties with rival courts.

sentences.zh: 雖曆偽朝，而不豫亂，世以此高之。

translations.literal: Though passing through puppet courts he never joined turmoil—the age therefore esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: He served usurpers yet kept clean hands.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in harness.

sentences.zh: 何琦

translations.literal: He Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi

sentences.zh: 何琦，字萬倫，司空充之從兄也。

translations.literal: He Qi, courtesy name Wanlun, was elder cousin of Minister of Works He Chong.
translations.idiomatic: He Qi, styled Wanlun, was He Chong's cousin.

sentences.zh: 祖父龕，後將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kan served general of the rear army.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather He Kan led the rear army.

sentences.zh: 父阜，淮南內史。

translations.literal: His father Fu was interior steward of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Father He Fu governed Huainan interior.

sentences.zh: 琦年十四喪父，哀毀過禮。

translations.literal: Qi at fourteen lost father—grief wasted him beyond ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Fatherless at fourteen he mourned fiercely.

sentences.zh: 性沈敏有識度，好古博學，居於宣城陽穀縣，事母孜，朝夕色養。

translations.literal: Nature calm keen with judgment—loving antiquity broadly learned—dwelling in Yanggu county of Xuancheng—serving mother tirelessly morning and evening with joyful nurture.
translations.idiomatic: Bookish anchorite of Xuancheng—devoted son.

sentences.zh: 常患甘鮮不贍，乃為郡主簿，察孝廉，除郎中，以選補宣城涇縣令。

translations.literal: Often troubled delicacies insufficient—therefore became commandery chief clerk—nominated filial and honest—appointed gentleman-of-the-household—selected magistrate of Jing county in Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He took petty posts to feed mother.

sentences.zh: 司徒王導引為參軍，不就。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Wang Dao summoned him aide—did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He refused Wang Dao.

sentences.zh: 及丁母憂，居喪泣血，杖而後起，停柩在殯，為鄰火所逼，煙焰已交，家乏僮使，計無從出，乃匍匐撫棺號哭。

translations.literal: When mourning mother—dwelling in grief weeping blood—only rose with staff—bier awaiting burial—neighbor fire pressed—smoke and flame crossing—house lacked servants—no plan—therefore crawled embracing coffin wailing.
translations.idiomatic: Mother's funeral caught fire—he clung to the coffin weeping on the floor.

sentences.zh: 俄而風止火息，堂屋一間免燒，其精誠所感如此。

translations.literal: Soon wind ceased fire died—one hall room spared burning—such was sincerity's resonance.
translations.idiomatic: Wind shifted—the hall survived untouched.

sentences.zh: 服闋，乃慨然歎曰：「所以出身仕者，非謂有尺寸之能以效智力，實利微祿，私展供養。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he sighed deeply: "The reason I took office was not boasting petty skill to display wit—truly hoping humble salary might privately extend support.
translations.idiomatic: "After mourning he renounced office—parents gone.

sentences.zh: 一旦煢然，無復恃怙，豈可復以朽鈍之質塵默清朝哉！

translations.literal: Once utterly alone without reliance—how again employ blunt substance to stain silent Qing court!
translations.idiomatic: "Why polish ambition for an empty court?

sentences.zh: 」於是養志衡門，不交人事，耽玩典籍，以琴書自娛。

translations.literal: " Therefore nurtured intent at humble gate—no worldly dealings—immersed in classics—using zither and books for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: "He lived on classics and music.

sentences.zh: 不營產業，節儉寡欲，豐約與鄉鄰共之。

translations.literal: He did not manage estates—frugal few desires—sharing surplus and want with neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: He shared famine and feast with neighbors.

sentences.zh: 鄉里遭亂，姊沒人家，琦惟有一婢，便為購贖。

translations.literal: Township suffered turmoil—sister lost to another household—Qi had only one maid—thereupon purchased redemption.
translations.idiomatic: He sold his lone maid to ransom his sister.

sentences.zh: 然不為小謙，凡有贈遺，亦不苟讓，但于己有餘，輒復隨而散之。

translations.literal: Yet did not affect petty modesty—when receiving gifts never falsely declined—but whenever surplus remained promptly spread it abroad.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted gifts only to give them away.

sentences.zh: 任心而行，率意而動，不占卜，無所事。

translations.literal: Following heart in action—moving by inclination—no divination—no attachments.
translations.idiomatic: He acted by conscience alone.

sentences.zh: 司空陸玩、太尉桓溫並辟命，皆不就。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Lu Wan and Grand Marshal Huan Wen jointly summoned—both refused.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wan and Huan Wen failed to recruit him.

sentences.zh: 詔征博士，又不起。

translations.literal: Edict summoned erudite—again did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial doctorate summons went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 簡文帝時為撫軍，欽其名行，召為參軍，固辭以疾。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jianwen was general pacifying armies admiring his name conduct summoned him aide—firmly declined citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jianwen wanted him—pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 公車再征通直散騎侍郎、散騎常侍，不行。

translations.literal: Court carriage twice summoned straight-speaking supernumerary gentleman attendant—did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Twice summoned court gentleman—ignored.

sentences.zh: 由是君子仰德，莫能屈也。

translations.literal: Therefore gentlemen admired his virtue—none could bend him.
translations.idiomatic: The elite idolized his stubborn virtue.

sentences.zh: 桓溫嘗登琦縣界山，喟然歎曰：「此山南有人焉，何公真止足者也！

translations.literal: Huan Wen once climbed mountain bordering Qi's county—sighed—"South of this mountain someone dwells—Lord He truly knows enough!
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen sighed that He Qi embodied contentment.

sentences.zh: 」琦善養性，老而不衰，布褐蔬食，恆以述作為事，著《三國評論》，凡所撰錄百許篇，皆行於世。

translations.literal: " Qi skilled nurturing nature—old without decay—wearing cloth eating vegetables—always taking composition as task—authored "Critiques of Three Kingdoms"—writings exceeding hundred pieces—all circulated in age.
translations.idiomatic: "He wrote histories and essays past eighty.

sentences.zh: 年八十二卒。

translations.literal: Died age eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 吳逵

translations.literal: Wu Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kui

sentences.zh: 吳逵，吳興人也。

translations.literal: Wu Kui was a man of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kui hailed from Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 經荒饑疾病，合門死者十有三人，逵時亦病篤，其喪皆鄰里以葦席裹而埋之。

translations.literal: Passing famine hunger pestilence—whole household thirteen died—Kui then gravely ill—burials all neighbors wrapped in reed mats.
translations.idiomatic: Famine killed thirteen kin—neighbors buried them in rush mats.

sentences.zh: 逵夫妻既存，家極貧窘，冬無衣被，晝則傭賃，夜燒磚甓，晝夜在山，未嘗休止，遇毒蟲猛獸，輒為之下道。

translations.literal: Kui couple surviving—home utterly destitute—winter lacked bedding—day hired labor—night fired bricks—day and night on hills never resting—meeting venom insects fierce beasts always yielding road.
translations.idiomatic: Destitute pair fired bricks by night and labored by day among beasts.

sentences.zh: 期年，成七墓、十三棺。

translations.literal: Within a year completed seven tombs thirteen coffins.
translations.idiomatic: In one year he raised seven tombs for thirteen dead.

sentences.zh: 時有賻贈，一無所受。

translations.literal: Whenever condolence gifts came—accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: He refused funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 太守張崇義之，以羔雁之禮禮焉。

translations.literal: Prefect Zhang Chong honored him—using lamb and goose ritual courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhang Chong honored him formally.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: Died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historian's appraisal.
translations.idiomatic: Closing commentary by the historians.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：尊親之道，禮經之明訓；

translations.literal: The historians say: honoring kin is luminous teaching in ritual canon;
translations.idiomatic: Historians: honoring parents anchors ritual;

sentences.zh: 孝友之義，詩人之美談，是知人倫之本，罔茲攸尚。

translations.literal: filial friendship's meaning—the poets' lovely discourse—thus knowing human bonds' root—none surpass this reverence.
translations.idiomatic: filial devotion defines human ethics.

sentences.zh: 盛翁子立行淳至，素蓄異才，流慟致其感通，含哺申其就養，戴昌賞其清韻，陸雲嘉其茂德。

translations.literal: Sheng Wengzi established conduct pure utmost—inborn strange talent—streaming tears achieved spiritual resonance—mouth-feeding extended nurture—Dai Chang prized his clear tones—Lu Yun praised his lush virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yan moved heaven with tears.

sentences.zh: 王裒隱居不從其辟，行己莫逾其禮，枯柏以應其誠，驚雷以危其慮。

translations.literal: Wang Pou hid recluse refusing summons—conduct none surpassed ritual—withered cypress answered sincerity—thunderbolt threatened his care.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pou's thunder oath shook readers.

sentences.zh: 永言董蔡，異時均美。

translations.literal: Forever speaking Dong and Cai—different eras equal beauty.
translations.idiomatic: He ranks with Dong Yong and Cai Shun.

sentences.zh: 許孜少而敏學，禮備在三，馴雉棲其梁棟，猛獸擾其庭圃，居喪之禮，實古今之所難焉。

translations.literal: Xu Zi young yet keen learning—rites fulfilled among three relationships—tamed pheasants nested beams—fierce beasts roamed garden—mourning rites truly hard ancient and modern.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zi's mourning moved birds and beasts.

sentences.zh: 庾叔褒不匱表於執勤，則裕存乎敬業，幽顯不易其操，疫癘不駭其心，急病讓夷之規，有古人之風烈矣。

translations.literal: Yu Shubao showed inexhaustible zeal in duties—then abundance rested in reverent work—hidden and manifest never shifted resolve—plague never shook heart—yielding danger ancient hero's measure—he possessed ancient awe.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Gun modeled plague-era courage.

sentences.zh: 孫晷之匪懈，王談之復仇，神人惜其亡，良守宥其罪。

translations.literal: Sun Gui's tirelessness—Wang Tan's revenge—spirits pity his death—good prefect pardoned crime.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Gui and Wang Tan moved gods and judges alike.

sentences.zh: 劉殷幼丁艱酷，柴毀逾制，發三冬之堇，賜七年之粟，至誠之契，義形於茲。

translations.literal: Liu Yin young bore cruel hardship—wasting flesh beyond measure—sprouted winter purslane—granted seven-year grain—utmost sincerity's covenant—righteousness appeared herein.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin's miracles fed scholars.

sentences.zh: 王延叩冰而召鱗，扇席而清暑，雖黃香、孟宗，抑為倫輩。

translations.literal: Wang Yan knocked ice summoning fish—fanned mats clearing heat—even Huang Xiang Meng Zong rank peers.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan rivals Huang Xiang's filial lore.

sentences.zh: 其餘群子，並孝養可崇，清風素范，高山景行，會其宗流，同斯志也。

translations.literal: Remaining gentlemen alike—filial nurture worthy reverence—clean breeze plain model—high mountain bright deed—gather their currents—share this intent.
translations.idiomatic: All exemplars join one humane chorus.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：德之所屆，有感和征。

translations.literal: Encomium says: where virtue reaches—responses sense and summon.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: virtue draws heaven's echo.

sentences.zh: 孝哉王許，永慕烝烝。

translations.literal: Filial Wang and Xu—forever longing harmoniously.
translations.idiomatic: How Wang and Xu longed endlessly.

sentences.zh: 揮泗凋柏，對榥巢鷹。

translations.literal: Wiping tears withered cypress—facing lintel nesting hawk.
translations.idiomatic: Tears stained trees where hawks nested.

sentences.zh: 密、彥、夏、庾，夙標至性。

translations.literal: Mi, Yan, Xia, Yu—early marked utmost nature.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi, Sheng Yan, Xia Fang, Yu Gun showed pure hearts.

sentences.zh: 文度、弘都，勤修懿行。

translations.literal: Wendu and Hongdu—diligently cultivated lovely conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Gui and Yan Han polished grace.

sentences.zh: 敦彼孝友，載光謠詠。

translations.literal: Encourage those filial friends—brightening songs and hymns.
translations.idiomatic: Their friendship lit every ode.

sentences.zh: 鳩馴長盛，魚薦延元。

translations.literal: Doves tame at Changsheng—fish offered Yanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin's doves and Wang Yan's fish blessed heirs.

sentences.zh: 談桑義闡，琦吳道存。

translations.literal: Tan clarifies mulberry righteousness—Qi preserves Wu teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tan and Sang Yu carried humane truth.

sentences.zh: 專洞之德，咸摛左言。

translations.literal: Focused penetrating virtue—all wielded these histories.
translations.idiomatic: Their purity fills these annals.
